Reports conflict over whether that penalty is dominated by non-radiative recombination at laser scribing margins, by convective drying instabilities generating coffee-ring solute segregation, or by heterogeneous out-of-plane residual lattice strain across the bulk film. Operational stability verification remains sparse and fragmented across all architectures: only 39 publications designated a standardized consensus protocol from the International Summit on Organic Photovoltaic Stability (ISOS), and only 39 studies reported an operational lifetime metric, with the longest duration reaching 4100 h under continuous illumination. Reporting rigor varies widely across device families, in that 52.1% of published abstracts state an efficiency value, yet only 8.5% report independent certification, representing just 114 certified works across the surveyed corpus. Progress in perovskite photovoltaics has therefore decoupled from uncertified efficiency metrics, and has shifted toward coupled ionic-electronic degradation under operating electrical and thermal stress. Resolving buried contact degradation between out-of-plane molecular desorption and lateral field-induced dewetting requires operando bias-dependent sum-frequency generation and conductive atomic force microscopy. Settling open-circuit voltage (Voc) losses demands operando drive-level capacitance profiling (DLCP) coupled with depth-resolved photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) mapping, to distinguish true defect passivation from electrostatic band realignment.
items.authors: Havid Aqoma

items.title: Conformational ensembles of the TDP-43 NTD-RRM1-RRM2 domains interacting with GU-rich RNA determined by MD simulations and SAXS data
items.abstract: TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) is a crucial regulator of RNA metabolism whose pathological aggregation is a hallmark of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), and Alzheimer’s disease. Binding to GU-rich RNA sequences via its RNA recognition motifs (RRM1 and RRM2) is known to antagonize aggregation, yet the molecular mechanisms by which RNA modulates TDP-43 conformational and supramolecular organization remain poorly understood. This limitation arises from the challenges related to the structural resolution of the inter-domain dynamics by experimental methods due to the protein intrinsically disordered regions, notably the linker connecting the N-terminal domain (NTD) to RRM1. To address this gap, we performed a combined all-atom (AA) and coarse-grained (CG) molecular dynamics (MD) investigation of a TDP-43 NTD–RRM1–RRM2 monomer in both the absence and presence of GU-rich RNA. AA simulations were carried out using the protein AMBER03ws and RNA AMBERχOL3 force fields to accurately capture protein–RNA 1 interactions. In parallel, we developed a MARTINI 3–compatible CG model for GU–rich RNA and performed CG simulations to access longer timescale conformational dynamics and extend structural trends observed with atomic accuracy. Small-angle X–ray scattering (SAXS) data were integrated to refine the conformational ensembles generated by both AA and CG simulations using the genetic algorithm judging optimization of ensembles (GAJOE). Across resolutions, our results consistently show that RNA binding reshapes the conformational ensemble of TDP-43. RNA association promotes closer packing of the RRM domains while subtly modulating the spatial arrangement of the NTD. Importantly, the ensemble refinements improve the agreement with experimental SAXS data without altering the underlying residue-level protein–protein and protein–RNA interaction network, suggesting that the conformational dynamics of the NTD-RRM1 intrinsically disordered linker is not affected by the RNA binding. As a first step toward the modeling of TDP-43–RNA oligomeric assemblies, this work establishes a validated multi-scale framework for studying the impact of RNA binding on TDP-43 self-assembly and supramolecular organization. By bridging AA atomic details, CG conformational sampling, and integration of experimental data for ensemble refinement, our approach provides accurate insight into how RNA binding regulates domain organization and conformational heterogeneity of TDP-43, shedding light onto its role in proteinopathies.
items.authors: Zichen Feng, Cagla Okyay, Aurélien Thureau, David Pastré, Ahmed Bouhss, Liuba Mazzanti

items.title: Experimental Data Analysis and Improved Cytochrome P450 Site-of-Metabolism Prediction for Drug Discovery
items.abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes mediate the oxidative metabolism of most marketed drugs, making early prediction of their sites of metabolism (SoMs) essential for addressing metabolic liabilities. In this work, we present a substantial update to our hybrid docking/quantum mechanics SoM prediction tool IMPACTS (J. Chem. Inf. Model., 2012, 52, 2471-2483). This update is evaluated on newly curated, fully annotated datasets containing over 2,400 datapoints and spanning nine human isoforms; these datasets are released to the community in MOL2 and JSON formats. Technical implementations presented in this work include 1) development of a three-dimensional solvent-accessible surface area correction to the precomputed activation energies, 2) design and integration of a highly efficient L-BFGS optimizer, and 3) elimination of a filter that had been historically used to remove unproductive binding modes. We follow these updates with extensive benchmarking and analysis on the newly curated datasets, where we show 1) achievement of a global Top-2 accuracy of ~75% across the nine isoforms and 2) the effective computational cost using the new optimizer was less than 1 minute per metabolite for eight of the nine isoforms. Finally, we present six real-world case studies comprised of approved drugs and discontinued clinical candidates. These case studies illustrate both the practical value and the remaining limitations of our approach.
items.authors: Mihai Burai-Patrascu, Antoine Moitessier, Matej Janezic, Anne Labarre, Kevin Cusack, Joshua Pottel

items.title: Large Language Models in Chemistry and Materials Science: A Comprehensive Survey
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are expanding the scope of artificial intelligence in chemistry and materials science by connecting scientific knowledge, heterogeneous data, computational tools, and experimental workflows. This article presents a comprehensive survey of the foundations, representations, methods, applications, and evaluation of LLM-centered scientific systems. We develop a non-exclusive representation-by-mechanism taxonomy linking text, molecular and crystal structures, spectra, images, and numerical properties with model adaptation, cross-representation grounding, external knowledge and tools, and workflow coordination. Within this framework, we synthesize prompting, domain pre-training and fine-tuning, preference alignment and verifier-driven reinforcement learning, multimodal integration, and retrieval- and agent-based approaches. Applications span literature understanding, property prediction, molecular and materials design, synthesis planning, characterization, hypothesis generation, and closed-loop discovery. By linking method choices to input information, task definitions, and validation conditions, the framework clarifies which reported results can be compared and what scientific claims they support. We organize representative datasets and benchmarks and introduce an evaluation matrix connecting task performance with information fidelity, uncertainty, chemical and physical validity, and workflow reliability. Detailed supplementary cases document the settings and evidence underlying key comparisons. Finally, we identify research priorities in integrated scientific representations, efficient adaptation, reusable knowledge and tool interfaces, and verifiable human-machine collaboration. By linking methodological developments to scientific objectives, this survey provides a conceptual map and practical guidance for developing and assessing LLM-enabled chemical and materials discovery.
items.authors: JINSHI LI, CHENGCHUN LIU, CHENGRUI WEI, YIMI WANG, BOXUAN ZHAO, ZHIYUAN YAN

items.title: Certified Zero-Frequency Response and a Fourth-Order Mechanism Test for Nonlinear Soft-Constrained Langevin Dynamics
items.abstract: Eliminating stiff internal coordinates can preserve equilibrium while changing kinetics, and a finite-time coarse-graining error does not by itself control a zero-frequency transport observable. We study a reversible overdamped Langevin model with constant microscopic mobility and nonlinear soft constraints, Uϵ(x, y; γ) = V (x− Fγ) + |y − g(x)|2 2ϵ , where V may be nonquadratic and nonconvex. An exact coordinate transformation factorizes the equilibrium measure but produces a nontrivial kinetic metric. For any mean-zero source depending only on x, we prove a direct zero-frequency comparison between the full microscopic inverse response Rϵ and the constrained geometric response R0: 0 ≤ R0 −Rϵ ≤ ϵmT 2 Eπ∥Dw0∥2F , where w0 is the source-specific corrector derived from the effective Poisson equation. The bound contains no inverse global spectral gap. For a one-dimensional translated potential, the conjugateforce friction closes explicitly and admits a certified first finite-stiffness correction with two-sided O(ϵ2) remainder bounds. We then derive a mechanism test: any autonomous hidden-history model for which two-time forces are conditionally standard Gaussian with history-dependent correlation must have a nonnegative connected fourth quantity K4(t). A fully reversible nonlinear constant-mobility Langevin model violates this condition: K4,ϵ(t) 0 for a nonzero short-time interval at every finite ϵ, while its constrained limit satisfies K4(t) 0 for every t 0. The all-time sign is certified by a five-dimensional outward-rounded interval Schur test controlling the infinite even sector of the generator. Integer interval arithmetic, independent primal–dual calculations of the full two-dimensional process, and a reversible finite-volume discretization provide mutually distinct checks. These results are a controlled response and model-discrimination theory for a specified soft-constrained class; they do not constitute a general theory of glass formation or a bulk shear-viscosity prediction.
items.authors: Yueer Yang

items.title: Seedless one-pot synthesis of high aspect ratio chiral gold nanofibers
items.abstract: Chirality, a fundamental characteristic of nature, plays a decisive role in molecular recognition, catalysis, and cellular organization. Translating this asymmetry into synthetic systems has the potential to unlock new functionalities at the interface of nanoscience and biology. Here, we report the synthesis of high-aspect-ratio chiral gold nanofibers, a class of one-dimensional chiral plasmonic materials, fabricated via a seedless, soft-templated, ligand-assisted growth method using D/L-cysteine as chiral inducers. Small-angle X-ray diffraction and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy results support the hypothesis of a soft template-mediated growth mechanism. The resulting chiral gold nanofibers exhibit pronounced, mirror-symmetric circular dichroism signals and characteristic plasmonic resonances, confirming their intrinsic structural chirality. Further, 4D scanning transmission electron microscopy analysis indicates that the atoms arrange in a chiral fashion, resulting in the observed topographical chirality of the gold nanofibers. Altogether, this effort establishes a simple and scalable route to fabricate chiral gold architectures with potential applications in asymmetric catalysis, optical sensing and bio-instructive scaffoldings.
items.authors: Mathias R. S. Nielsen, Rebekka Klemmt, Espen D. Bøjesen, Marcos López Hernández, Jan Skov Pedersen, Miguel Alexandre Ramos-Docampo

items.title: Performance Self-Blown Non-Isocyanate Polyurethane Foams
items.abstract: Rigid foams earn their place in structural applications through a specific balance of stiffness and density. Reproducing that balance without isocyanates has proven far harder than replacing the chemistry itself. Water-blown polyhydroxyurethane (PHU) foams are the most credible isocyanate-free alternatives to conventional polyurethanes, but toxic base catalysts and weak mechanical properties have stalled their adoption. Brønsted acid catalysis, long dismissed on the expectation that amine protonation suppresses urethane formation, proves effective instead: a dynamic equilibrium of transient protonation and thermal amine regeneration widens the rheological window for water-driven CO2 release while carrying the network to full conversion. Acidic conditions additionally activate vinyl ethers, converting the pendant and vicinal hydroxyls responsible for moisture plasticization into acetal crosslinks. The resulting poly(hydroxyurethane)–polyacetal (PHU–PAC) foams show a sixteenfold (16x) higher rubbery modulus, a fourfold higher compressive modulus (4 → 18 MPa), and halved water uptake relative to the PHU benchmark. Normalized peak heat release rate falls nearly eightfold below that of a commercial PU foam, and on an Ashby plot of specific strength versus stiffness, PHU–PAC approaches HDPE and PVC. Addressing catalyst tractability, moisture uptake, and mechanical performance in one formulation, acid-catalyzed PHU–PAC reframes non-isocyanate foams as tunable structural materials and positions catalyst design as a lever for the next generation of sustainable cellular materials.
items.authors: Gabriel Perli, Guillem Seychal, Bruno A. Piscelli, Yi Wang, Maliheh Razavi-Esfali, Lucas Polo Fonseca

items.title: Interfacial Solvent Engineering of Zinc Porphyrin Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Frameworks Enables Aggregation-Enhanced Electrochemiluminescence for Synthetic Cannabinoid Sensing
items.abstract: Zinc porphyrin hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (ZnTCPP HOFs) are prone to uncontrolled short-range π–π stacking at solid/liquid interfaces, which leads to aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) and consequently limits their electrochemiluminescence (ECL) efficiency. Current strategies for suppressing ACQ primarily depend on covalent or coordination bonds and often involve laborious synthesis. Addressing this challenge from the perspective of colloid and interface science, this study introduces a chitosan (CS)–DMF counter-solvent precipitation strategy. This approach reorganizes the hydrogen-bond network and fosters electrostatic association between CS and the carboxyl groups of ZnTCPP HOFs, thereby facilitating a controlled transformation of bulk crystals into micro/nano-aggregates. This synergistic effect suppresses short-range π–π stacking while enhancing long-range aggregation-induced emission (AIE), leading to a significant improvement in ECL efficiency without the need for an additional co-reaction promoter. On this basis, an aptamer-based ECL sensor was developed for the ultrasensitive detection of 5F-EDMB-PINACA, achieving a limit of detection of 8.61 × 10 -16 g/L and a linear range spanning nine orders of magnitude. These findings underscore the efficacy of colloidal-interface regulation in ECL sensing.
items.authors: Yanpei Zhang, Ding Jiang, Bingxue Fan, Mingyang Han, Suran Tian, Haibo Li

items.title: RaX-DT: An Open-Source Platform for Automated Molecular Docking Workflows and Reproducible Pipeline Validation
items.abstract: Automated molecular docking workflows often fail not at the scoring engine but at the interfaces between ligand preparation, protein preparation, binding-site definition, and post-processing. We present RaX-DT, an open-source, Docker Compose–deployable platform that integrates these steps in a single web application and an optional conversational assistant. RaX-DT automates 3D ligand generation, tautomer/protonation-state handling, protein cleaning, binding-site definition via P2Rank, Fpocket, or user-specified coordinates, GNINA-based docking, and interactive result visualization. Because end-to-end automation can introduce silent failures, we validated the assembled workflow on 231 protein–ligand co-crystal structures from DUD-E and LIT-PCBA rather than treating the docking engine in isolation. Of these, 186 structures completed successfully; the top-ranked pose reproduced the crystallographic pose within 2.0 Å for 65.1% of completed structures, and the best of the five top-scoring poses reached 77.4%. Validation also exposed a box-placement defect that would have produced plausible-looking but invalid output, underscoring the value of pipeline-level quality control. RaX-DT is released under the MIT license and is intended to improve accessibility, reproducibility, and transparency in routine docking workflows.
items.authors: Amir Hosein Ghavi, Bita Barazandeh Shirvan, Zohre Ganji, Zahra Jafari, Mojgan Nejabat, Farzin Hadizadeh

items.title: Synthesis and Ambiphilic Reactivity of a Monocoordinate Carbazolyl Gallylene
items.abstract: Monocoordinate Lewis base-free gallium(I) complexes are rare due to their high propensity for disproportionation and oligomerization. Herein, we report the synthesis and structural characterization of a monomeric, monocoordinate gallylene stabilized by a bulky 1,8-bis(3,5-ditert-butylphenyl)-3,6-di-tert-butylcarbazole ligand. Taking advantage of the substantial kinetic shielding provided by the flanking aryl substituents, the compound can be isolated as a solvent free, one-coordinate main-group carbenoid. With a lone pair and two vacant p-orbitals, this compound features an ambiphilic character which was experimentally probed through coordination to both Lewis-acidic transition-metal fragments (M(CO) 5 ; M = Cr, Mo, W) and strong σ-donor Lewis bases, including the N-heterocyclic carbene ( IPrMe NHC) and 4-dimethylaminopyridine (DMAP). Furthermore, the Ga(I) complex shows oxidative addition of methyl iodide and phenanthrene-9,10-dione. Conversely to other monocoordinate gallylene compounds its carbometallation reactions are kinetically and thermodynamically unfavored.
items.authors: Nasrina Parvin, T. Ilgin Demirer, Dennis Welterlich, Bernd Morgenstern, Alexander Hinz, Diego M. Andrada

items.title: Study of neutron-induced effects on cultural heritage linen fabrics using fluorescence spectroscopy
items.abstract: This study investigates how the fluorescence of linen changes when it is irradiated with a focus for the first time on the distinction between neutron from pure gamma ray irradiation. Earlier studies showed that when linen was subjected to both neutron and gamma irradiation, its visible and ultraviolet (UV) fluorescence increased as the radiation dose increased. However, the spectroscopic reason was not explained, and the specific contributions of neutrons versus gamma rays were not addressed. In this work, a particular linen is used as a control, and the changes caused by irradiation are characterized and analyzed using steady-state and time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy, as well as total UV fluorescence photography. The tests reveal that only neutrons, and not gamma rays, increased UV fluorescence in linen. The different ways in which the two forms of radiation interact are highlighted. In addition, the spectral ratio between the yellow band and the blue band areas, as well as the time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy, could indicate that the linen was exposed to neutrons. The results support cluster-triggered emission (CTE) as the main cause of cellulose autofluorescence as a constituent of linen, and also a relative increase of CTE with the neutron dose. Finally, the underlying mechanisms of the visual fluorescence perception are analyzed, and the observed effect is explained by calculating the L dimension of the fluorescence spectra using the CIE L*a*b* color space. This work proposes a simple device for detecting neutron irradiation in place in cultural heritage linen fabrics, with potential applications in conservation and forensic analysis.
items.authors: César Barta, María Fernández-Álvarez, Marta Liras, Elisa María Ruiz-Navas

items.title: Collaborative Laboratory Edge Networks
items.abstract: Chemistry language models now predict reactions and retrosynthetic routes with useful accuracy, but they assume that proprietary reaction records can be pooled into a central cluster and that inference runs on abundant accelerators. Neither assumption holds in pharmaceutical and fine-chemical practice, where yield records cannot leave the plant network, the points of use are heterogeneous resource-limited sites, and different laboratories occupy disjoint regions of chemical space. We present ChemFedFusion, a heterogeneity-aware framework for federated chemistry-model training and offloading over collaborative laboratory edge networks. ChemUCP is a chemistry-aware utility–cost predictor that scores a task–node pair by expected chemistry gain, expected latency, and an explicit out-of-distribution risk of emitting unparsable or unreliable chemistry, using a dual-channel tokenizer and a scaffold-coverage encoder that is corrected online from execution feedback. CSAW replaces sample-count aggregation with the product of a scaffold-space complementarity term, a site reliability term, and a weakened volume guard, amplifying rare chemistry while suppressing noisy sites. ARCO couples offloading and aggregation through a shared adaptation matrix and an event-driven asynchronous aggregator with a staleness bound, so that successful offloads teach the aggregator which node is competent for which chemistry task. On Mol-Instruction and USPTO-50K, ChemFedFusion reaches 0.883 Exact and 51.36% Top-1, and on the FedChem suite it reduces regression RMSE by up to 9.99% and classification ROC-AUC improvements are consistent across all nine datasets and three heterogeneity levels. The framework reduces convergence rounds by 22.4% and raises the fraction of answers that are both on time and chemically valid by 8.8 percentage points. A failure analysis shows that the remaining errors are dominated by synthetically infeasible routes that parse correctly, which no validity-based router can detect.
items.authors: Andre Williams, Shanice Brown, Kevin Thompson, Jamar Campbell, Alicia Morgan

items.title: Alternative synthetic pathways to selected molecular fluorophores present in citric acid-based carbon dots
items.abstract: Molecular fluorophores (MFs) are an integral part of many raw reaction mixtures prepared during the synthesis of carbon dots (CDs) from small organic molecules by the bottom-up methods. Despite their significant contribution to the luminescence of as-prepared CDs, the investigation of optical properties of MF is complicated by the pH dependence, possibility of formation of tautomers, low yields and complicated isolation. In this review, we summarize the structure of MFs detected in CDs prepared from citric acid (and various dopants), whose structure contains pyridin-2(1 H )-one ring annulated to 5- or 6-membered heterocycles. These compounds are closely related to citrazinic acid (CZA). The second part of the review deals with the alternative synthesis pathways towards ring-fused 2-pyridones, that could be used to prepare analogous compounds without the drawbacks related to the direct synthesis from CA (formation of carbonaceous matrix along with MFs resulting in low yields). MFs prepared by alternative pathways, free from polymerized and carbonized particles, could be used as standards towards better understanding of optical properties of CDs.
items.authors: Alex Sedlařík, Jela Nociarová

items.title: Redirecting Iodine Oxidation in Thyroxine by O-Phosphorylation
items.abstract: nachtsheim@uni-bremen.de Abstract O-Phosphorylation of a thyroxine derivative redirects mCPBA oxidation from the internal iodine to a terminal one. A two-step oxidation-hydrolysis sequence delivers the phosphate-stabilised aryl(hydroxy)iodonium salt, whose regiochemistry is established by 3 J-CP-coupling.
items.authors: Marcel Sancken, Felix Schindler, Boris J. Nachtsheim

items.title: From Automated Beamlines to Autonomous Science
items.abstract: Autonomous experimentation is emerging across materials synthesis, synchrotron and neutron characterization, real-time analysis, and scientific decision-making. Yet increasingly capable artificial intelligence does not by itself create autonomous science. Scientific user facilities must also provide machine-operable experiments, machine-readable and interoperable data and interfaces, persistent provenance across the experimental lifecycle, scientific capabilities that can be discovered and orchestrated across instruments and facilities, and access models compatible with iterative experimental campaigns. We argue that these infrastructure requirements should be treated as a coupled scientific design problem. Their value is not limited to higher throughput: reducing the latency between observation, interpretation, decision, and the next measurement can make metastable states, competing phases / phase coexistence, degradation, failure pathways, phase boundaries, and other difficult-to-access phenomena experimentally observable. Drawing on recent demonstrations in autonomous laboratories and advanced characterization, along with discussions from the 2026 Advanced Light Source Automation and Self-Driving Labs Workshop, we outline a practical progression from automated instruments to distributed autonomous discovery ecosystems that link synthesis, synchrotron and neutron characterization, computing, theory, and human scientific judgment.
items.authors: Chenhui Zhu, Marcus M. Noack, Wiebke Koepp, Thomas Ferron, Oleg Kostko, Damon English

items.title: Exploration of Low-Crystalline NiPd(CN)4 by Ab Initio Global Structure Search
items.abstract: For poorly crystalline inorganic materials, it is often difficult to uniquely determine the crystal structure from diffraction measurements alone. In this study, we identified the crystal structure of a newly synthesized metal cyanide NiPd(CN) 4 by combining experiments with ab initio calculations. The observed powder X-ray diffraction pattern could not be explained by any previously reported analogous structures, while magnetization measurements indicated the presence of a finite local magnetic moment in the ground state. Using these experimental constraints as clues, we obtained a relaxed tilt structure with distorted square-planar coordination through heuristic structure modeling, and discovered a µ-bridged structure, in which Ni adopts a six-coordinate octahedral environment, through ab initio global structure search. The candidate structures were comprehensively validated through comparisons between theory and experiment for powder X-ray diffraction, Raman scattering, XAFS, STEM, and UV–vis spectroscopy, and the µ-bridged structure was found to reproduce the experimental results well. Based on these findings, we conclude that the µ-bridged structure is strongly suggested to be the realized structure of NiPd(CN) 4 .
items.authors: Ryunosuke Fujimaru, Yuudai Iwai, Haruka Yoshino, Hitoshi Miyasaka, Koji Kimoto, Yusuke Nambu

items.title: Investigating pH Effects on the Photoswitching of Furanyl-Indolinium Heteroarylstilbenes
items.abstract: Cationic heteroarylstilbenes, such as the furanyl-indolinium chromophore, represent a class of watersoluble, visible-light-responsive photoswitches. However, their photochemical behaviour under physiologically relevant pH conditions remains insufficiently understood. In this study, four derivatives were synthesized and systematically investigated, with particular emphasis on their photoswitching properties at three pH values using phosphate-buffered media. The visible-light-induced E/Z photoisomerization kinetics were analysed by UV/Vis spectroscopy, while the structures of the resulting isomers were confirmed by NMR spectroscopy. A key result is the pronounced pH dependence of the thermal Z→E back-isomerization in phosphate buffer, whereas the photoinduced E→Z switching is only weakly affected. The apparent thermal recovery is superimposed by a competing dark-decay process, which was quantified independently to separate concurrent degradation from the actual thermal back-isomerization kinetics. The derivatives differ in their chemical stability. The methyl-substituted derivative is comparatively robust, whereas the nitro-substituted derivative shows pronounced degradation. These results show that water solubility alone does not guarantee robust photoswitching under biologically relevant conditions and that both pH-dependent switching kinetics and chemical stability must be considered in the design of cationic heteroarylstilbene photoswitches.
items.authors: M. Seemann, J. N. Riese, R. Geitner, A. G. Groß, Alexander Gross

items.title: Designing Cure Kinetics in Polyester Networks: Tuning Initiator Content to Control Gelation and Glass-Transition Development
items.abstract: Unsaturated polyester networks remain widely used in composite manufacturing, construction, and infrastructure, and yet the practical relationship between initiator content and cure trajectory is not always reported consistently across industrial formulations. Using a field-representative unsaturated polyester systems, real-time gelation/exotherm were tracked with differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) to map how initiator type and content govern gel time, exotherm behavior, and the thermal state of the cured network. Across the compositions examined, gel time varied roughly four-fold, from approximately 10–12 minutes to 44–45 minutes, and peak exotherm temperature reached approximately 123–137 °C. Across an extended 0.8–4% peroxide range, the first-scan glass transition (Tg1) rose from 46.15 to 56.38 °C and residual cure enthalpy (ΔH) fell from 33.35 to 15.67 J/g, while the fully cured glass transition (Tg2) rose sharply to approximately 100–103 °C at intermediate peroxide content before declining to 84.74–89.20 °C at 3–4%. These results indicate that additional initiator can accelerate cure and reduce measured residual reaction while not necessarily improving the final thermal state of the network.
items.authors: Parastou Kharazmi

items.title: VIBE-QC: an open-source, general-purpose electronic-structure code for molecules and solids developed with generative AI
items.abstract: We present VIBE-QC, a general-purpose open-source electronic-structure code for molecules and solids, developed almost entirely through generative-AI-assisted programming (“vibe-coding”) under expert human direction. The molecular stack provides Hartree–Fock and Kohn–Sham DFT over the full LIBXC library, analytic gradients and Hessians, Møller–Plesset theory and double hybrids, coupled cluster with local-correlation variants, multireference methods, excited states, dispersion, continuum solvation, effective core potentials, and semiempirical methods. The periodic stack treats one-, two-, and three-dimensional systems at multiple 𝒌 through three Fock-build routes. Production claims are validated by out-of-process cross-code comparisons against established reference programs, reaching the nanohartree scale for mean-field methods and 3.3 × 10−7 𝐸h for conventional CCSD(T); external parity for periodic total energies is open work at this release, tracked in the public issue tracker. VIBEQC adds a container-based results-storage and visualization format (QVF), an interactive viewer (VIBEVIEW), and a job queue (VIBE-QUEUE), under the MPL-2.0 license. Graphical TOC summary. VIBE-QC is an open-source, general-purpose electronic-structure code for molecules and solids that was built almost entirely through generative-AI-assisted programming under expert direction, and validated capability-by-capability where production status is claimed. It spans Hartree–Fock through coupled cluster, multireference, and excited states for molecules, and three periodic Fock-build routes for solids, and ships its own modern file format (QVF), viewer (VIBE-VIEW), and cluster-aware queue (VIBE-QUEUE).
items.authors: Michael F. Peintinger

items.title: Direct visualization of heterogeneous molecular diffusion and interfacial barriers during condensate ripening
items.abstract: Ripening processes are ubiquitous in various multiphase systems, such as emulsions, crystals, alloys, and biomolecular condensates. This phenomenon significantly affects the morphology of a system and its resulting properties through the growth of dispersed domains at the expense of others without direct contact. Though ripening has been studied for centuries, a molecule-level visualization of this process has never been captured, significantly hindering our fundamental understanding. Here, we use single-molecule tracking techniques to visualize and quantify the diffusion dynamics of poly-L-lysine (PLL) during a rapid ripening process, where ATP droplet condensates transform into fibrillar crystals. We successfully observe preferential motion of PLL within both the dilute and condensate phases toward growing crystals and uncover previously unknown molecular dynamics near interfaces. At condensate interfaces, PLL molecules encounter energetic barriers that trap their motions and restrict their escape from condensates. Near crystal fibers, we discover clear heterogeneity in molecular dynamics, which can be classified into Brownian, confined, and superdiffusive motions. To explain this result, simulations and a physical model reveal the formation of water lubrication layers on crystal fibers, which enables PLL molecules to slide along fibers with superdiffusive motion before crossing the layer and becoming immobilized on fibers with confined motion. These results provide molecular-level insight for understanding the fundamental ripening process and answering open questions across diverse nonequilibrium systems.
items.authors: Feipeng Chen, Arman Moussavi, Christopher Rademacher, Danielle Tullman-Ercek, Sinan Keten, Muzhou Wang

items.title: Enhancing Grignard reactions via anion borrowing in deep eutectic /organic biphasic media
items.abstract: The rational optimization of the Grignard reaction remains a considerable challenge for synthetic chemists. When assessing nucleophilic additions to unsaturated organic molecules, it has been shown that improved performance can be achieved using deep eutectic solvents (DESs). In this case, a solution of the Grignard in THF is added to the DES containing the substrate under vigorous stirring. In this study, we determine the underlying causes for this beneficial effect by combining ab initio molecular dynamics, QM/MM simulations, and enhanced sampling, using i -PrMgCl and acetophenone as reagents, THF as the organic solvent, and a 1:2 solution of choline chloride:glycerol as the DES. Our results show an increased preference for the Grignard reaction over the formation of by-products originating from a β-H transfer from the isopropyl group with the DES/THF media. This enhanced selectivity stems from the formation of chlorinated dimagnesium entities at the DES interface. While the reaction of a neutral Grignard in bulk THF kinetically favours the β-H transfer, the chlorine enrichment originating from the DES is shown to make the two reactions kinetically more equivalent, and to drastically favor the thermodynamic preference for the Grignard product, a result of increased intramolecular stabilizing interactions. This result is in line with experimental evidence of increased selectivity in the presence of various halide salts. This mechanistic interpretation paves the way for the rational improvement of Grignard reagents, allowing an even broader application of these compounds in these non-conventional solvents.
items.authors: Marco Bortoli, Eva Hevia, Odile Eisenstein, Michele Cascella

items.title: Nanothermodynamic Generalization of the Young–Laplace and Young Equations for Sessile Droplets with Line Effects
items.abstract: Thermodynamic investigations of wetting phenomena require that we handle the nanoscale. By combining Hill’s small-system thermodynamics with a Gibbsian composite-system description, we formulate the equilibrium thermodynamics of a sessile nanodroplet. We consider a one-component liquid droplet resting on an ideal, flat, inert solid substrate and in contact with reservoirs that fix the temperature and chemical potential. Finite-size effects are retained in the liquid bulk phase, the liquid–vapor interface, and the three-phase contact line, while the solid–vapor and solid–liquid interfaces are assumed to follow regular thermodynamics and treated macroscopically. The distinction between integral and differential pressure, surface tension, and line tension is used to derive nanothermodynamic generalizations of the Young–Laplace and Young equations. The resulting equations account for the size-and shape dependence of the finite thermodynamic contributions and recover the classical equilibrium equations in the macroscopic limit.
items.authors: Vitor H. C. Cunha, Signe Kjelstrup, Dick Bedeaux

items.title: Multimodal Representation Learning for Exploring Natural Product Chemical Space
items.abstract: Natural products represent a major source of therapeutic molecules, yet their structural diversity and limited biological annotations pose substantial challenges for computational exploration and discovery. Here, we develop a multimodal molecular representation framework that integrates chemical language, molecular fingerprints, physicochemical descriptors, and molecular graphs into a unified latent space for natural product discovery. Using structurally out-of-distribution molecular spaces, we show that molecular representation and sampling strategy jointly determine which regions of chemical space are explored. Multimodal pretraining captured chemically informative representations that enabled exploration of structurally unseen natural products, while comparisons with singlemodality representations showed that representation advantages depended on the discovery objective rather than being universally superior. The pretrained representation was transferable across anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activity predictions, and its integration with active learning enabled data-efficient exploration of biologically active molecules. Prospective evaluation of structurally unseen natural products further connected model-guided exploration with experimental antioxidant activity. These findings establish molecular representation and sampling as coupled determinants of chemical-space exploration and show
items.authors: Tarapong Srisongkram, Supreeya Paiboon, Huynh Anh Duy

items.title: Molecule–Metal Nanostructure Interactions in Plasmonic Chemistry
items.abstract: Plasmonic chemistry converts metal nanostructures into photocatalysts via three interconnected channels at the molecule–metal interface: enhanced near fields, non-equilibrium charge carriers, and localized heat. This review focuses on this interfacial perspective. We show how adsorbates and ligands do more than just stick to nanoparticles – they reduce plasmon lifetimes, change work functions, modify the density of states, and impact the energy and charge flow during various physical processes. Ultrafast thermalization under pulsed excitation and steady state conditions under continuous illumination open up different pathways for chemical reactions. Although the plasmonic metal is crucial, surface-bound molecules actively participate by scavenging charge carriers, affecting selectivity and stability, and even undergoing chemical transformations. These aspects are crucial for controlling product distributions and enabling novel chemical pathways by exploiting excited-state pathways inaccessible through thermal energy. Together with the nanoscale properties of plasmonic nanostructures, chemical reactions can be confined to nanoscale hot spots shaped by geometry and polarization. These insights inform the development of practical design principles for antenna–reactor hybrids and novel plasmonic materials in which absorption, carrier localization, and interfacial alignment are precisely engineered. Finally, we identify key open questions and the need for operando interfacial techniques to transform these insights into practical tools for selective, solar-driven synthesis.
items.authors: Sergio Kogikoski Junior, Wouter Koopman, Felix Stete, Radwan M. Sarhan, Shashank K.Gahlaut, Evgenii Titov

items.title: Incoherent Transport Signatures in Ferrocene and Ferrocenium-based Molecular Wires
items.abstract: Molecular wires incorporating redox units are foundational to single-molecule electronics, yet the molecular designs and environment which govern whether charge-transport proceeds predominantly via phase-coherent quantum tunnelling or thermally activated incoherent hopping remains debated. By synthesising bench-stable Fe(III) ferrocenium wires ( ex-situ oxidation) and comparing their molecular conductance against electrochemically gated Fe(II) analogues ( in-situ oxidation) within scanning tunnelling microscopy break-junctions, we identify distinct experimental signatures of coexisting transport regimes. For both ferrocene and ferrocenium systems, while phase-coherent tunnelling through frontier molecular orbitals dominates at low bias, favourable environmental reorganisation energetics trigger efficient, two-step sequential processes at high biases. These findings resolve a long-standing mechanistic question in metallocene molecular electronics and highlight how two-terminal measurements alone are insufficient to resolve such ambiguities. Our combined electrochemical approach provides a pathway to more robust characterisation of transport phenomena in molecular junctions.
items.authors: Linlin Hou, Varshini Kumar, Munirah Alsaqer, Amit Sil, James M. F. Morris, Chongguang Liu

items.title: Reply to a comment ‘On the futility of the Fuoss–Kirkwood relation’ by Gradišar Boškoski
items.abstract: A recent comment on our previous paper (Electrochem. Commun. 164 (2024) 107731) regarding the futility of the so-called Fuoss-Kirkwood (FK) relation presents an appreciated opportunity for clarification and further argumentation. In this reply, we provide additional arguments suggesting that the commenting authors are misguided in concluding that this relation is valid, and that, when correctly applied, the FK relation can be straightforwardly employed to derive analytical expressions of the real-valued distribution of relaxation times (DRT) for model impedances that are explicitly known in closed form and do not possess ω-domain singularities. Moreover, we present analytical expressions of the DRT for the impedances of the Cole-Cole (CC) and Havriliak-Negami models, which are generally complex-valued, and validate their accuracy by incorporating them into the DRT integral equation with a Debye kernel, utilising the proven sifting property of the δ distribution.
items.authors: K T Malkow, Thomas Malkow

items.title: Atomic Orbital Interactions in [CeX6]2– (X = F, Cl, Br): Consequences for X-Ray Absorption Spectroscopic Analysis
items.abstract: Metal–ligand bonding in [CeX 6 ] 2– complexes (X = F, Cl, Br) is investigated using density functional theory (DFT) and pre-bonding analysis. The analysis quantifies atomic orbital (AO) energies and overlaps in the complexes, with a focus on the mixing between Ce 4f AOs with halide 𝑛p donor AOs. Results indicate that decreasing Ce–ligand AO overlap from X = F to Br is compensated by improved AO energy matching, leading to increased 4f-based ligand-to-metal donation across the series. Population analysis derived from pre-bonding data rationalizes recent experimental X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) findings. Effective orbital overlaps extracted from XANES data using a simplified AO bonding model based on the Wolfsberg–Helmholtz (WH) relation are compared directly with pre-bonding overlaps. The consequences of using ionization potential (IP) based AO energies in the experimental data workup and other assumptions inherent in the bonding model are also scrutinized. Using consistent pre-bonding AO energies in the model requires a WH constant of 𝐾 ≃ 3 to reproduce the calculated overlaps for 4f-based interactions. Combining IP-based AO energies with a conventional value 𝐾 = 2, as done in prior studies, is shown to yield comparable overlaps due to a cancellation of errors. Overall, pre-bonding analysis provides a framework rooted in first-principles theory for connecting AO interactions in the molecule with experimental bonding trends.
items.authors: Kurtis Stanistreet-Welsh, Jacob A. Branson, Stefan G. Minasian, Jochen Autschbach

items.title: Influence of Structural Flexibility on Ion-Receptor Interactions in Octamethyl Calix[4]pyrrole Complexed with Prolinate
items.abstract: We present cryogenic ion vibrational spectroscopy of deprotonated L-proline ([Pro-H]-) complexed with octamethyl calix[4]pyrrole (omC4P). Density functional theory calculations reveal two low-energy binding motifs. In the lowest energy structure, the carboxylate group interacts with only three NH groups of omC4P, with the NH group of the fourth pyrrole pointing away from the binding site. In another geometry, slightly higher in energy, the ion binds to all four NH groups. The experimental IR spectrum matches the lowest energy isomer, featuring a free NH stretching signature at 3439 cm-1 alongside strongly red-shifted NH stretching modes involving the three strong hydrogen-bonding NH groups. This three-point binding motif represents a departure from the typical four-point binding observed with smaller anions, demonstrating how the charge distribution of the guest and the structural flexibility of the receptor affect binding of larger anions. Despite the reduced number of hydrogen bonds, the three-point binding motif is lower in energy due to shorter, stronger hydrogen bonds, and it is the dominant motif of [Pro-H]-·omC4P in vacuo.
items.authors: Lane M. Terry, J. Mathias Weber

items.title: When the lower-barrier pathway yields the minor enantiomer: reversibility and intermediate stability in pyrroloindoline synthesis
items.abstract: In this work, we present a computational study that provides evidence for the origins of selectivity in the enantioselective synthesis of pyrroloindolines catalyzed by iminium ions. Through a conformational search combined with DFT calculations, we obtained the catalytic energy profile, which shows that the enantioselectivity is not determined by the barriers of the enantiodetermining C–C bond-forming step. A microkinetic model built on this profile reproduces the experimental enantiomeric excess and identifies the origin of the selectivity: under conditions in which the steps preceding product release are reversible, the catalyst-bound intermediate I9 accumulates preferentially along the S pathway, where it is markedly more stable than its R counterpart. The selectivity therefore reflects a thermodynamic contribution operating at the level of the diastereomeric on-cycle intermediates rather than a difference in activation barriers. We stress that this outcome is not accessible from the free energy profile alone: a simple inspection of the activation barriers predicts the opposite sense of induction, and only the explicit kinetic treatment reproduces the experimental results. Previous studies have suggested that control of the E/Z ratio of the iminium ion intermediate was related to catalytic selectivity; here we show that the stereoinduction originates from the predominance of the E isomer of the iminium ion. Furthermore, for the C–C bond-forming step, we identify the regions of the system involved in the noncovalent interactions that govern selectivity. Finally, by introducing substituents on the substrate, we observe a decrease in the activation barrier associated with the iminium ion–substrate interaction when electron-donating groups are present in the nucleophile.
items.authors: Felipe Schoma Cardoso, Bruno Matos Paz, Ataualpa A. C. Braga

items.title: Enhancing Linear B-Cell Epitope Prediction via Evolutionary Scale Modeling (ESM-2) and Hybrid Feature Integration
items.abstract: Experimental identification of B-cell epitopes is time-consuming and resource-intensive, motivating the adoption of computational prediction approaches. This study examines the progression of sequence-based strategies by contrasting traditional machine learning methods (SVM, XGBoost, etc.) and early deep learning techniques (CNN, RNN, etc.) with sophisticated protein language models such as ESM-2. By systematically evaluating multiple feature encodings, including amino acid composition, dipeptide composition, k-mer tokenization, and evolutionary embeddings, we established that capturing both global semantic context and local sequence motifs is essential for robust predictive performance. Optimal performance was achieved using a hybrid framework that combined 15B-parameter ESM-2 embeddings with k-mer features. This hybrid approach achieved an AUC of 0.743 and an MCC of 0.333 on independent validation using an Extra Trees classifier, and an AUC of 0.738 and an MCC of 0.356 using an XGBoost classifier on the same dataset. Our findings indicate that transformer-based embeddings yield enhanced protein representations; however, their predictive efficacy is optimized when integrated with local motifs and ensemble learning, presenting a scalable, high-accuracy alternative to conventional and standalone deep learning frameworks.
items.authors: Prasun Pal, Sai Jahnavi Pasumarthi, Sandipan Chakraborty

items.title: Black-Body-Based Scatter Removal Procedure for Quantitative Neutron Radiography at the MARS Beamline (CG-1D), HFIR
items.abstract: Quantitative neutron imaging is fundamentally limited by scattering artifacts, low neutron flux, and wavelength-dependent attenuation, which restrict accurate transmission measurements. This work presents the first implementation and validation of the blackbody (BB) based scatter removal procedure (Carminati et al., 2019) for quantitative neutron radiography of engineering materials at the MARS beamline (CG-1D), High Flux Isotope Reactor (HFIR), Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL). The scatter removal pipeline was applied to a series of single crystal nickel (Ni) and polycrystalline austenitic (γ-phase) 316L stainless steel samples pre-charged with hydrogen gas (H2) at pressures of 1.5, 5, 12.5, and 20 kpsi. The BB correction removed a spatially varying scatter contribution of up to 8% of the local transmission that was not eliminated by conventional open-beam normalization. After scatter removal and subtraction of the metal-matrix attenuation, the resulting H attenuation coefficient, µH, increased monotonically with H concentration in both materials. Ni exhibited a higher H attenuation response than 316L stainless steel, consistent with differences in H solubility and trapping behavior. Pixel-wise maps further revealed concentration-dependent spatial heterogeneity, including localized regions of elevated µH in Ni at the highest H concentration. At the lowest concentrations, uncertainty in the interpolated scatter field exceeded the spatial-sampling uncertainty and established the effective detection floor of the measurement. Independent validation experiments were performed at the VENUS beamline of the Spallation Neutron Source using a H-free 316L stainless steel sample as a control and a water column with a known H number density as a reference standard. The corrected measurements recovered the expected zero H signal in the control and the H attenuation of the water reference, demonstrating that the pipeline can distinguish H attenuation from matrix and scatter contributions across independent beamline conditions. These results establish a validated workflow for removing sample dependent scatter and enabling quantitative analysis of neutron radiography data acquired at cold-neutron imaging beamlines.
items.authors: Dayeeta Pal, James Torres, Yuxuan Zhang, Hassina Bilheux, Jean-Christophe Bilheux, Zipeng Xu

items.title: Chemical Synthesis of the endogenous metabolite Phosphocitrate and Its Structural Isomer Phosphoisocitrate
items.authors: Petri Turhanen

items.title: Why Molecular-Scale Occupancy Fluctuations Appear Gaussian without Being Bulk-Like
items.abstract: Molecular-scale occupancy distributions in water and hard-sphere fluids can appear remarkably Gaussian. Using classical density functional theory with an external field conjugate to the occupancy, we calculate occupancy cumulants for spherical volumes in a hard-sphere fluid and reproduce the variance and small, oscillatory third moment reported previously in Monte Carlo simulations. This agreement shows that the density functional captures the correlations responsible for the phenomenon and allows the role of excluded-volume packing to be isolated. By comparison with the Poisson limit and by varying both observation-volume size and bulk density, we show that excluded-volume correlations strongly suppress the higher cumulants. The resulting skewness and excess kurtosis remain nonzero and oscillatory, but they become small as the observation volume increases. However, over the same molecular-scale range, the finite-volume variance remains strongly scale-dependent and does not attain the extensive scaling set by the bulk compressibility. The early onset of near-Gaussianity is therefore governed primarily by molecular packing: it does not demonstrate that the fluctuations have reached the thermodynamic Gaussian limit, nor does it support a distinct small-cavity regime governed by bulk-like Gaussian fluctuations.
items.authors: Nigel B. Wilding

items.title: A theory of inner-sphere reorganization energy for electrocatalysis
items.abstract: In Marcus theory, reorganization energy links thermodynamics and kinetics for outer-sphere electron transfer, in which the redox centre exchanges an electron without changing its bonding to the electrode. Most electrocatalytic elementary steps are instead inner-sphere processes: the reacting intermediate is part of the interface, and surface bonding changes with charge transfer. A general thermodynamic definition of the full nonequilibrium preparation cost of such a bonded interface is lacking, leaving equilibrium descriptors and measured rates without a common theoretical basis. Here we define this quantity thermodynamically and provide a first-principles procedure for its calculation. A Legendre transform of fixed-potential thermodynamics yields an internal free-energy surface in which interfacial polarization and surface bond state are coupled variables, while electrode potential remains an external control. For a specified elementary event, inner-sphere reorganization energy is the finite free-energy cost of preparing a product-like interface before relaxation. Writing this cost as a Bregman difference separates it from the reaction driving force and relates it to a weighted integral of local interfacial stiffness. The classical Marcus expression is recovered as the one-dimensional harmonic charge-only limit of this framework. Applied to Volmer hydrogen oxidation on
items.authors: Kaicong Yang, Bing Huang, Lin Zhuang

items.title: Why Electrochemical–Thermal–Mechanical Understanding is Needed to Explain Knees in Lithium-Ion Batteries Degradation
items.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are essential to modern life, spanning portable electronics, electric vehicles and grid storage. Yet, their degradation mechanisms remain incompletely understood, particularly the sudden capacity drops known as knee points. In this study, commercial Samsung 50S cells are degraded under various cooling setups and charge/discharge rates, revealing consistent knees in slow-discharge cells even above 80% of initial capacity, while fast-discharge cells degraded beyond 60% without knees. Using a multiphysics characterisation approach, we decipher the origins of these knees: attainment of lower voltages enhances silicon activity, triggering a chain of mechanisms that culminate in sudden failure. Specifically, recurring SEI reformation drives a dual pathway: gas release displaces electrolyte, inducing localised current concentration, overcharge and a first pattern of lithium plating, while simultaneous electrode thickening deforms the jelly roll. This mechanical effect, combined with geometrical heterogeneities from the welded tab design, produces a second pattern of lithium plating in later ageing states, identified as the primary cause of the knees. These findings elucidate the complex coupling of multiscale degradation mechanisms and demonstrate that robust state-of-health monitoring must be holistic, incorporating indicators beyond traditional temperature, capacity and resistance.
items.authors: Matheus Leal de Souza, M. Waseem Marzook, Mohammed Asheruddin N, Derek Siu, Antonis Vamvakeros, Gregory Offer

items.title: Zeolite-Mediated Three- and Pseudo-Five-Component Reactions Involving α-Ketoglutaric Acid, Aromatic Aldehydes and 5-Aminotetrazole
items.abstract: We report previously undescribed multicomponent reactions of α-ketoglutaric acid, aromatic aldehydes, and 5-aminotetrazole that provides access to two distinct types of products. Notably, these transformations require the presence of 4A or 3A molecular sieves, and the formation of the target compounds is condition-controllable: the process can proceed through a pseudo-five-component pathway, yielding tetrahydropyrido[3,4-d]tetrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidinone derivatives – the first examples of this heterocyclic framework – or can be directed toward a three-component condensation that affords dihydrotetrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine dicarboxylic acids. The latter were identified as key intermediates in the pseudo-five-component transformation, enabling the synthesis of pyrido[3,4-d]tetrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine systems via a two-step Doebner-type and Castagnoli–Cushman-type/decarboxylation sequence with an expanded range of possible substrates, thereby combining tetrazole, dihydropyrimidine, δ-lactam, and triazole pharmacophore motifs within a single fused framework.
items.authors: Vladyslav O. Honcharov, Valentyn A. Chebanov, Olena H. Shvets, Vyacheslav E. Saraev, Svitlana V. Shishkina, Yana I. Sakhno

items.title: Macromolecular Size Matching in Stabilizing Corrugated Chiral Plasmonic Nanostructures
items.abstract: Chiral plasmonic nanoparticles derive strong chiroptical responses sensitive from their corrugated, high-curvature surfaces, but these same features are thermodynamically unstable. Surface functionalization using macromolecules could broaden their utility by enabling improved colloidal compatibility, secondary functionalization, stimuli responsiveness and and assembly into higher-order structures. However, as the chiroptically active surface feactures are often only a few nanometer in size, inadequate size matching leads to structural instability, causing particle surfaces to flatten and consequently diminishing their chiroptical properties. Here, we show that chain-length-selective polymer functionalization stabilizes the fine groove structures of chiral gold nanorods. We identify a threshold behavior of hydrodynamic diameter below which polymer coils can penetrate and anchor within the grooves, preserving structural integrity and chiroptical activities. Guided by this principle, we establish a sequential functionalization strategy using polymers of two distinct sizes to produce chiral AuNRs with stable chiroptical performance. Our results establish a general design rule for integrating versatile macromolecular architectures with chiral nanoparticles and expand the engineering space for nano-optical applications.
items.authors: Yingying Cai, Anjana Kannan, Jessica Ma, Qun Song, Yuwen Peng, Kai Zhang

items.title: Reducing Synthetic Complexity: A Fluorine-Free Benzodithiophene-Thienopyrrolodione Donor Polymer by Direct Arylation Polycondensation for Organic Photovoltaics
items.abstract: Synthetic complexity is a decisive aspect for absorber material availability in organic photovoltaics (OPVs). By using direct arylation polycondensation (DAP), a new route to the donor polymer PBDT-T2-TPD is presented. DAP allows to reduce the amount of toxic chemicals and simplifies the reaction scheme at the same time. Furthermore, this new route allows to vary the molar mass of PBDT-T2-TPD and thus enables the investigation of chain length-dependent OPV parameters in devices with the non-fullerene L8-BO as acceptor. An increasing molar mass results in an improvement of the open-circuit voltage, the fill factor and the power conversion efficiency, while the short-circuit current density saturates after an initial increase. These changes arise from reduced non-radiative voltage losses and enhanced mobility–lifetime products. The performance of the best performing DAP material is at least as

items.title: Aged Hops Increase 3-Methyl-2-butene-1-thiol (MBT), β-Ionone, and Branched-Chain Esters in Beer
items.authors: Toru KISHIMOTO

items.title: A bench-scale, continuous reactor for reductive polyolefin depolymerization
items.abstract: Catalytic deconstruction of polyolefins is central to chemical recycling, but most laboratory studies use batch reactors that obscure kinetics and limit reproducibility. Flow operation enables rigorous measurement of rates and selectivities, yet processing viscous polymer melts at small scales remains challenging. Here we present a laboratory-scale flow reactor that couples a hydraulic melt pump to a stirred-tank vessel, enabling continuous and semi-continuous operation at high pressure. The system achieves pseudo-steady state, where volatile production rates reflect C–C scission kinetics, validated by a first-principles model. Using this reactor with H-ZSM-5, we demonstrate three features of polyethylene hydrocracking difficult to probe in batch systems, namely that alkene selectivities exceed batch reactions by nearly tenfold, hydrogen availability within the melt governs the balance between alkene and alkane products, and catalyst acidity and crystallite size jointly tune this product balance through intermediate diffusion from the zeolite. This reactor provides a platform for kinetic and mechanistic studies of catalytic polymer deconstruction.
items.authors: Griffin Drake, Juliana Lu-Yang, Anna E. Brenner, Joel Miscall, Gregg T. Beckham, Yuriy Román-Leshkov

items.title: Quantifying Validation-Induced Optimism in Machine Learning for Food Spectroscopy: An Empirical Multi-Dataset Benchmark
items.abstract: Background: Evaluating machine-learning regression models in food spectroscopy using random row-wise cross-validation ignores hierarchical experimental structures (replicate scans, aliquot extractions, packaging batches, instruments, and harvest campaigns). While theoretical warnings caution against sample leakage, the chemometric literature lacks a multidataset empirical quantification of validation-induced optimism, its impact on model selection, and its underlying physical mechanisms. Methods: We executed an empirical multi-dataset benchmark across four benchmark food spectroscopy collections encompassing 12,706 source spectra/records, with 6,376 spectra evaluated in primary regression workflows: Cargill corn near-infrared (NIR; n = 240 spectra across 80 physical grain samples and 3 spectrometers; targets: moisture and protein), edible vegetable oils Raman (Gilbraith , 2024; n = 215 spectra across 52 distinct reference titration determinations; target: peroxide value), mango fruit dry matter NIR (Anderson , 2020; n = 4,233 calibration spectra across 5 cultivars and n = 1,448 external harvest season spectra; target: dry matter content), and Tecator meat NIR (n = 240 spectra with 24 duplicate pairs [48 rows participating in identical pairs], leaving 216 unique spectral profiles; targets: fat and moisture). Six regression algorithms—partial least squares (PLS), Ridge regression, support vector regression (SVR-RBF), Random Forest, XGBoost, and k-nearest neighbours (kNN, serving as a diagnostic sentinel)—were evaluated across four hierarchical validation tiers: Level 1 (random row-wise cross-validation), Level 2 (sample-aware group cross-validation, reference-valuegrouped validation, or deduplicated validation), Level 3 (cultivar-aware validation), and Level 4 (external instrument and seasonal holdout). Model specifications were held fixed across validation tiers to isolate validation design as the sole manipulated factor, and all spectral standardisation was strictly fitted within training partitions to eliminate unsupervised leakage. Results: Transitioning from random row-wise to structured validation systematically eroded apparent predictive performance across all 36 random-to-structured model–task contrasts, yielding a median validation-induced optimism ΔR2 of 0.0170 (mean 0.3290, interquartile range [0.0084, 0.3985]) and a median root-mean-square error inflation ratio (RR_RMSE = RMSE_structured / RMSE_random) of 1.1395 (mean 1.4277, IQR [1.0417, 1.4374], range [0.9406, 5.2645]). Degradation was especially pronounced under external domain transfer (median ΔR2 = 0.6399, median RR_RMSE = 1.8199). In edible oils containing replicate scans sharing identical titration reference values, random cross-validation produced catastrophic performance inflation for non-linear models: kNN collapsed from an apparent R2 of 0.8865 (RMSE 5.40 meq O2/kg) to −2.1443 (RMSE 28.43 meq O2/kg; RR_RMSE = 5.265), and Random Forest collapsed from R2 = 0.8437 to −0.5806 (RR_RMSE = 3.180). This replicate leakage completely inverted algorithm rankings (Spearman ρ = −0.886, p = 0.019; Kendall τ = −0.733, p = 0.056). Algorithm robustness under external transfer was domain-specific: Ridge was the most resilient model under Mango seasonal transfer (R2 = 0.6690, compared to R2 ≈ 0.13–0.17 for tree ensembles), whereas uncalibrated Corn instrument transfer caused severe degradation in linear models (Ridge R2 = −30.04, PLS R2 = −37.05) due to uncorrected spectrometer baseline shifts. In contrast, non-linear models exhibited smaller relative degradation under sensor transfer. Cross-partition nearest-neighbour spectral similarity dropped by up to 0.0164 under domain transfer. Across tasks, this similarity drop showed an exploratory positive association with kNN error inflation (Pearson r = 0.739, Spearman ρ = 0.912), consistent with a spectral-proximity mechanism whereby high optical similarity enables flexible models to interpolate training points rather than learning transferable chemical relationships. Conclusions: Random row-wise validation creates severe validation-induced optimism, distorts algorithm rankings, and rewards models that memorise experimental artefacts. Reporting standards, mandatory specimen-level split manifests, and the routine inclusion of kNN as a diagnostic canary are essential to restore methodological integrity and field deployability to machine learning in food analysis.
items.authors: Ketney Otto

items.title: Crowding-induced interfacial aggregation underlies enzyme concentration-dependent inhibition during poly(ethylene terephthalate) depolymerization
items.abstract: Enzymatic depolymerization of poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) using PET hydrolases (PETases) offers a sustainable route for plastic recycling, yet high enzyme loadings paradoxically reduce degradation efficiency. The molecular basis of this enzyme concentration-dependent inhibition (ECDI) has remained unresolved. Here, by exploiting host-dependent differences in folding quality of a sequence-identical PETase, we show that ECDI is driven by crowding-induced interfacial aggregation, which progressively destabilizes PET-bound enzymes. By establishing aggregation propensity as a tractable design parameter, we demonstrate a complementary multi-level engineering framework operating at the sequence, folding, and reaction-environment levels that suppresses interfacial aggregation and improves PET depolymerization across multiple PETases. Our findings reveal how enzyme–enzyme interactions can govern catalytic performance at heterogeneous solid–liquid interfaces, providing a mechanistic basis for designing high-performance biocatalytic systems under high-enzyme-loading conditions.
items.authors: Eon Ji Jo, Byung Hoon Jo

items.title: Transferable Graph Neural Network Surrogates for Molecular Dynamics Across Crystal Symmetries
items.abstract: We present a transferable graph neural network (GNN) surrogate framework for molecular dynamics (MD) that directly predicts atomic displacements and propagates atomistic configurations without explicit force evaluation or numerical time integration. The central objective of this work is to establish whether a common GNN formulation can represent atomic dynamics across materials with fundamentally different crystal symmetries and coordination environments. The same network architecture, feature representation, graph construction, and training protocol are applied without symmetry-specific modification to face-centered cubic (FCC) aluminum, body-centered cubic (BCC) iron, and hexagonal close-packed (HCP) magnesium. Across these distinct elemental and crystallographic systems, the framework achieves position-prediction errors on the order of 10−4 Å 2 and supports stable autoregressive propagation to nanosecond time scales. The predicted trajectories preserve thermodynamic stability, characteristic coordination-shell structure in the radial distribution functions, and temperature-dependent mean-squared-displacement behavior. In particular, the framework captures the closely spaced coordination shells of BCC iron and the anisotropic coordination environment of HCP magnesium without introducing lattice-specific representations. These results demonstrate that direct GNN-based atomic propagation can be formulated as a transferable framework across different elements, lattice symmetries, and coordination geometries, providing a pathway toward generalizable surrogate models for accelerated molecular dynamics.
items.authors: Judah Immanuel, Avik Mahata, Aniruddha Maiti

items.title: Electrochemically Hole-catalyzed Dearomative (3+2) Cycloaddition of Nitroarenes
items.abstract: We report the first electrochemically hole-catalyzed (3+2) dearomative cycloaddition of nitroarenes, including benzene-based derivatives. Enabled by a hole-transfer chain process, the reaction proceeds through the anodic generation of a non-stabilized azomethine ylide from a readily available precursor, providing efficient access to structurally complex pyrrolidines from a broad range of electron-deficient nitroarenes. Remarkably, full conversion is achieved using catalytic amounts of electricity (0.1 F mol-1), resulting in high TONe (222) and Faradaic efficiency (925%). This work expands the scope of hole electrocatalysis beyond electron-rich olefins and establishes a new platform for electrochemical dearomative cycloadditions. The scalability of the method was further demonstrated under continuous-flow conditions.
items.authors: Nathan Noël, Youssou Faye, Julien Legros, Laëtitia Chausset-Boissarie, Isabelle Chataigner

items.title: Fiber-Scale Discrete Element Modeling Approach for Microstructural Evolution in Carbon Felt Electrode Manufacturing
items.abstract: Porous carbon components strongly influence transport, kinetics, and performance in electrochemical energy devices, like electrodes in redox flow batteries or gas diffusion layers in proton exchange membrane fuel cells. Yet quantitative links between industrial felt manufacturing and the resulting microstructure remain insufficiently understood. Recent studies have explored alternative bottom-up fabrication strategies to achieve greater microstructural control, while computational optimization often considers stochastic microstructures without accounting for manufacturability. Consequently, the extent to which conventional manufacturing processes can tailor microstructure remains unclear. Here, we develop a discrete element method framework that resolves fiber-scale interactions and microstructural evolution during mechanical processing of oxidized polyacrylonitrile precursor felts. The framework represents successive stages of fiber generation, web formation, web laying, needle punching, and calendering. At each stage, the evolving three-dimensional microstructure is resolved and quantified using fiber- and pore-scale descriptors, including pore-size distributions, fiber-orientation tensors, and transport-related properties. The simulations reveal process–structure–transport relationships, identifying key parameters governing pore-throat size, fiber reorientation, and effective diffusivity. These findings define the microstructural design space accessible through conventional felt manufacturing and provide a basis for future process optimization and integration with subsequent thermal-processing stages.
items.authors: Arjun Sankar, Abhilash Valisammagari, Francisco Fernandez, Alejandro A. Franco

items.title: The first approach to highly substituted dihydroimidazotriazolones and their controlled post-transformations
items.abstract: A novel class of azido-modified α , β -unsaturated Ugi adducts (enamides) has been explored as a versatile platform for post -Ugi transformations. While intramolecular azide-alkyne cycloadditions of Ugi-derived peptidomimetics have been extensively studied, the corresponding azide-alkene cycloadditions on similar scaffolds have remained unexplored. In this work, we report a systematic investigation of intramolecular azide-alkene cycloaddition involving activated enamide moieties derived from Ugi adducts. Enamides readily undergo catalyst-free intramolecular [3+2] cycloaddition under mild conditions to afford the previously unknown 3,3a,4-trisubstituted-3a,4-dihydro-3 H -imidazo[1,2-c][1,2,3]triazol-5(6 H )-one scaffold in high yields. This novel fused heterocyclic system was fully characterised and proved to be a highly versatile intermediate for divergent post -Ugi transformations. Fused dihydrotriazoles transformed into 3,5-dihydroimidazol-4-ones via an elimination of N 2 supplemented by acylamide migration. Additionally, base- or acid-mediated cascades enabled efficient one-pot access to aromatised 1,2,3-triazoles and open-chain triamides, respectively. In total, 4 generations of structural isomers and 2 other classes of compounds were involved in the work. The methodologies developed highlight the synthetic value of azido-modified enamides as divergent intermediates, providing rapid and controlled entry to structurally diverse nitrogen-rich heterocycles and peptidomimetics from simple Ugi adducts derived from α , β- unsaturated aldehydes.
items.authors: Vladyslav Vereshchak, Viacheslav Saraiev, Vladimir Musatov, Svitlana Shishkina, Valentyn Chebanov, Alexander Tsygankov

items.title: A conformational filter protocol for structures with topological symmetry
items.abstract: This paper presents an efficient conformational filter protocol for handling structures with topological symmetry implemented in the open-source molecular modelling program curcuma. This approach addresses the challenge of comparing molecular conformations in which symmetrically equivalent atoms may have different indices in the structure files. Descriptors that are independent of the storing order of the atoms (energy differences, rotational constants, and Vietoris-Rips (VR) persistence barcodes) are used to efficiently predict potential structural similarities before performing computationally expensive permutations on selected structure pairs using distinct permutation approaches implemented in curcuma or the external tool molalign. The filter protocol operates in three phases: 1) initial RMSD-based filtering and data-set-specific training of the atom index-independent descriptor thresholds, 2) permutation-based filtering using parameterised descriptors, and 3) final filtering using stored permutation vectors. Our evaluation using 395 complex conformations optimised at different levels of theory shows that although conformational geometries typically remain similar across different theoretical methods; their relative energies can vary significantly between different levels of theory. This highlights the importance of efficient conformational filtering in identifying structurally unique conformers, particularly when faster semiempirical quantum chemical methods are used, which might incorrectly evaluate certain conformers as energetically unfavourablein contrast to slower more accurate quantum mechinal methods. A key finding is that performing all possible RMSD calculations does not necessarily yield the optimal filtering result, as the final outcome depends significantly on the specific order of the structure comparisons.
items.authors: Conrad Hübler

items.title: Quality control measurement science: Point-of-care opioid compounding and personalized pain management
items.abstract: Traditional "one-size-fits-all" pharmacotherapy often fails to address the complex, highly individualized needs of patients undergoing opioid tapering, pain management, and withdrawal. While distributed and point-of-care (POC) additive manufacturing—such as 3D printing, semisolid extrusion, and drop-on-demand (DoD) deposition—enable agile, patient-specific dosing and multi-drug formulations, they introduce critical quality control (QC) challenges in facilities that often lack extensive laboratory infrastructure. We employed a quality by design (QbD) approach to identify the critical relationships between input materials, process parameters, and critical quality attributes (CQAs) and investigated a tiered series of atline, inline, and final-product QC measurement technologies for personalized pain management and opioid-tapering therapies. Using precision DoD liquid dispensers, various tunable dosage forms were produced, including injectable saline solutions, semi-solid extruded tablets, and oral films. These vehicles carried full and partial opioid agonists, opioid antagonists, and adjuvant withdrawal medications (fentanyl, buprenorphine, methadone, oxycodone, naloxone, diphenhydramine, promethazine, and 2 bupivacaine). The performance, speed, and selectivity of four analytical techniques were explored: microdrop UV-Vis spectroscopy, liquid chromatography-UV (LC-UV), handheld Raman spectroscopy, and chromatography-free direct analysis in real time triple quadrupole mass spectrometry (DART-TQ-MS). We characterized and quantified each manufactured dosage form by either single-point calibration (i.e., against a reference standard [RS] or quality control standard) or linear least squares regression. Analytical control strategies for quality control require balancing throughput, analytical capabilities and limitations, and specific medicine considerations. This work defined robust metrological pathways for safe, compliant, and personalized point-ofcare pharmaceutical production, bridging clinical pain management and opioid tapering guidelines with manufacturing quality assurance.
items.authors: Thomas P. Forbes, Zainab Altamimi, Jeffrey Lawrence, Elizabeth L. Robinson

items.title: Neutron Crystallography Maps the Interaction Landscape of Pseudomonas aeruginosa LecA with Deuterated Aromatic β-Galactoside
items.abstract: Aromatic derivatives of β-galactosides are potent inhibitors of the LecA lectin, a key virulence factor of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, involved in host recognition, tissue adhesion and biofilm formation. This opportunistic bacterial pathogen is considered a serious global health threat, particularly due to the emergence of multidrug-resistant strains.
