Anti-adhesive and anti-biofilm compounds represent promising alternatives or complements to conventional antibiotic therapies. The design of such pathoblockers requires detailed structural insights into their interactions with the target protein. Neutron macromolecular crystallography (NMX) provides complementary structural information to X-ray diffraction (XRD), by enabling the localization of hydrogen atoms, but typically requires the use of deuterium-labeled molecules. We developed a unique approach combining bacterial production of deuterated galactose and its functionalization with a deuterated phenyl group, resulting in the first synthesis of perdeuterated phenyl-β-galactoside, PheβGal-d16. The structure of the deuterated bacterial receptor LecA in complex with PheβGal-d16 was determined using neutron diffraction, providing experimental localization of hydrogen atoms involved in hydrophobic contacts with the Pro38 and Gln53 residues, and in the unusual T-shaped π-stacking interaction with His50. These observations rationalize the 10-fold affinity increase measured for an aromatic β-galactoside compared to galactose.
items.authors: Theodore Arnaud, Delphine Carry, Chloé Tatol, Juliette M. Devos, Lukas Gajdos, Philippe Lesot

items.title: Strategic Bromine Substitution in Aryl Aminoboranes Unlocks Photochemical Route to Narrow-Band Emitting Azaborines
items.abstract: The development of UV/deep-blue emitters with high color purity remains a central challenge in OLED research, where conventional fluorophores suffer from broad emission and triplet-harvesting systems compromise stability. Here we show that strategic ortho-bromine substitution in bis-aryl aminoboranes unlocks an intramolecular photo-cyclization that allows direct access to azaborine frameworks under mild conditions and near quantitative yield. The high triplet energy of the aminoborane precursors enables efficient population of the T1 state, triggering ring closure and suppressing the twisted intramolecular charge-transfer (TICT) behavior characteristic of the open scaffolds. The resulting azaborines display deep-blue to near-UV emission, with remarkably narrow bandwidths (FWHM down to 0.09 eV in solution and 0.04 eV in glassy matrix) and localized excited states (LE). A systematic library screening unveils the modularity of this approach and shows that cyclization rate correlate with spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and triplet-state localization on the B-N bond. This work establishes the first photochemical route to azaborines and provides a synthetically versatile platform for high-purity emitters, suited for next-generation optoelectronic applications.
items.authors: Alessio Bussolari, Nunzio Matera, Andrea Pellegrini, Nicolò Mazzini, Sven Reese, Wojciech Mróz

items.title: A Vanadium(II) Photosensitizer Delivered by Human Serum Albumin for Photodynamic Therapy
items.abstract: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is an established clinically approved treatment; however, the development of next-generation photosensitizers remains constrained by the reliance on scarce precious-metal scaffolds and poor pharmacological properties. Earth-abundant first-row transition metals offer an attractive alternative, but their application in PDT remains underexplored. Herein, we report the first vanadium(II) photosensitizer for PDT and show that its biological activity can be unlocked through loading into human serum albumin (HSA), a strategy intended to improve its pharmacological properties. The resulting HSA-bound complex showed negligible dark toxicity and induced pronounced light-dependent cytotoxicity upon blue- and red-light irradiation in human colon carcinoma cells. Mechanistic studies revealed that the HSAbound complex preferentially accumulates in lysosomes, where red-light irradiation triggers singlet oxygen generation and promotes apoptosis. This work establishes vanadium(II) complexes as a new class of photosensitizers for photodynamic therapy and opens new opportunities for the design of first-row transition-metal photosensitizers with improved photophysical properties.
items.authors: Zisis Papadopoulos, Aimée Marie Irgel, Alexandra König, Katja Heinze, Johannes Karges

items.title: Helical Polymers for Artificial Cell Engineering: Backbone-to-Droplet Reorganization in Polyacetylene-based Microdroplets
items.abstract: Biomolecular condensates provide a powerful framework for constructing artificial cells with crowded interiors and dynamic molecular organization. However, most synthetic condensates rely on flexible or intrinsically disordered macromolecules, leaving the role of conformationally defined synthetic polymers in liquid-liquid phase separation largely unexplored. Here, we introduce cationic helical polyacetylenes as structurally defined building blocks for coacervate-based artificial cells and investigate how their conformation governs condensate properties. Complexation with ATP generates spherical, liquid-like microdroplets that sequester small organic molecules and proteins from the surrounding solution while supporting enzymatic transformations. These coacervates exhibit substantially greater resistance to increasing ionic strength than those formed with their linear counterparts, a behavior associated with changes in the polyacetylene backbone upon ATP complexation. Moreover, combining helical and linear polyamines induces the heterogeneous partitioning of a hydrophilic molecular guest, accompanied by a transition from spherical to amorphous condensates. Together, these findings establish a direct link between polymer secondary structure and condensate stability, morphology, and molecular organization, highlighting conformationally defined synthetic polymers as versatile building blocks for artificial cell engineering.
items.authors: Bruno Delgado Gonzalez, Ivan Torreiro-Leon, Lucía Medín-Agraso, Lorena Sánchez-Domínguez, Manuel Míguez, Roberto J. Brea

items.title: Report – 4th Ontologies4Chem Workshop
items.abstract: The Ontologies4Chem workshop series brings together developers and users of chemical ontologies to align ontology initiatives with shared standards and approaches to semantic interoperability. The 4th Ontologies4Chem Workshop, organized by TIB in collaboration with the Beilstein-Institute, the NFDI4Chem Consortium, the NFDI4Cat Consortium, and the Physical Sciences Data Infrastructure (PSDI) took place from November 11 to 13, 2025 in Limburg an der Lahn (Hessen, Germany). The programme covered chemical ontologies and their applications on the first day, the ontological representation of chemical reactions and experimental workflows on the second, and the reuse and further development of ChEBI as the central resource for chemical entities on the third. Talks on RO-Crate, DCAT-AP+, and chemDCAT-AP added the provenance and packaging layer that complements ontologies in FAIR data workflows. A central outcome of the workshop is the introduction of the Ontologies4Chem Canon, a vision of a living, community-curated body of the essential ontologies for chemistry together with their design patterns and the discourse around them. It rests on modular, OBO-aligned design, reuse before creation, the IUPAC Gold Book as source of definitions, and ODK-based development and deployment pipelines, provided by the NFDI4Chem Terminology Service and related internally through SSSOM mappings. The hacking sessions initiated the migration of the CHEMINF ontology to an ODK-based infrastructure and led to a decision, taken together with the ChEBI team, to reincorporate disjointness axioms into the ChEBI release cycle. Presentations on ontology pre-training, ChemLog, and Chebifier 2 showed how ontologies and machine learning reinforce each other. A panel discussion with the ChEBI team identified sustainable, community-driven governance and funding as the decisive challenges for the field.
items.authors: Oliver Koepler, Philip Strömert, Johannes Hunold, Sabrina Krohm, Noura Rayya, Samantha Pearman-Kanza

items.title: Additive manufacturing of micro-architected carbide ceramics via molten salt conversion
items.abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) enables complex micro-architected geometries in metals 1–3 , polymers 4 and oxide ceramics 4–6 , yet its extension to non-oxide ceramics remains constrained by optical opacity and high-temperature densification. Carbide ceramics are challenging for particle-based vat photopolymerization (VPP), where strong absorption limits curing, while pressure-assisted densification, often required for high density, is incompatible with delicate architectures. A general route to fabricate dense micro-architected carbide ceramics without conventional sintering remains unavailable. Here we demonstrate molten salt-assisted additive manufacturing of carbide ceramics (MOSAIC), an AM framework that decouples geometric shaping from carbide formation. Thermoset polymer architectures fabricated by VPP are pyrolysed into architected glassy-carbon templates and converted into carbide ceramics through molten-salt-mediated reaction with transition metals. MOSAIC produces micro-architected TiC, VC, Cr 3 C 2 and TaC with relative densities above 95% and features down to ~20 µm, and extends to WC, ZrC and Mo 2 C. Conversion depth can be controlled from ~1 µm to tens of micrometres, yielding solid carbide struts or hollow architectures after carbon removal. Controlled oxidation converts these structures into TiO 2 , Cr 2 O 3 , V 2 O 5 and Ta 2 O 5 while preserving topology. By separating architecture definition from ceramic formation, MOSAIC enables photopolymerization-based manufacturing of transition-metal carbides and derivative oxides across micrometre-scale features and millimetre- to centimetre-scale architectures.
items.authors: Chiranjit Roy, Apurv Dash

items.title: Carbonylative Cross Couplings Promoted by a Metal Carbonyl Complex in Catalytic Amounts
items.abstract: Carbon monoxide is a highly valuable building block that enables the rapid construction of complex molecules like pharmaceuticals from simple and commercial precursors. However, the handling of CO requires special and elaborate precautions, since it is a highly toxic and odourless gas supplied in pressurized gas cylinders. To improve operations with carbon monoxide several CO surrogates including Mo(CO) 6 have been introduced, which form CO in enclosed gas reactors on demand. Herein, we report on the discovery of Fe 2 (CO) 9 as a highly efficient CO surrogate, which unlike preceding works is capable to transfer 8 out of 9 CO ligands onto the molecule of interest. This enables the application diiron nonacarbonyl in “catalytic amount” of 15 mol% with regard to the aryl halide coupling partner (100 mol%). The high synthetic value of the novel approach is witnessed by three different carbonylative cross couplings, syntheses of four pharmaceuticals and a head-to-head comparison with Mo(CO) 6 as gold standard.
items.authors: Djavid Mohammadi, Richard Tröltzsch, Jonas Surkau, Karsten Lüdtke, Peter H. Huy

items.title: Transitional Band Gaps During Polarization Switching in Wurtzite Ferroelectrics
items.abstract: The electronic band gap ( E g ) is commonly treated as a static materials property associated with an equilibrium crystal structure. Yet in functional materials whose operation involves field-driven structural transformations, the relevant electronic structure may evolve as the atoms traverse different configurations, with consequences for materials design and device reliability. Wurtzite ferroelectrics provide a compelling setting to examine this idea because polarization reversal requires substantial atomic rearrangement and unusually large electric fields that can approach dielectric breakdown. Here, using first-principles calculations, we track E g along atomistically resolved polarization switching minimum energy pathways in experimentally established Al 1−x Sc x N, Ga 1−x Sc x N, and Al 1−x B x N ferroelectric alloys. As cation-centered tetrahedra rearrange and invert during switching, the band gap decreases substantially relative to the equilibrium polar state, with reductions reaching approximately 30-40% in some compositions. Importantly, the minimum E g does not necessarily coincide with zero polarization or with the highest-energy configuration along the switching pathway, demonstrating that the energetic and electronic structure landscapes do not map trivially onto one another. Extending the analysis to 24 chemically diverse wurtzite compounds reveals transitional E g reductions ranging from negligible to nearly 50%. These results identify the minimum E g sampled along the switching trajectory as an important, material-specific descriptor of electronic robustness. The results also suggest an intrinsic contribution to transient excess conduction during switching and motivate future studies connecting transitional electronic structure to conductive domain walls and memristive behavior in ferroelectrics.
items.authors: Alice Brambati, Thi Nguyen, Cheng-Wei Lee, Bhawna Sahni, Geoff L. Brennecka, Prashun Gorai

items.title: Auto-healing Co(II)-based metallosupramolecular hydrogel of 3-amino-1-propanol as Low Molecular Weight Gelator: Investigations of morphological features, rheological dynamics, and stimuli-responsiveness
items.abstract: In the present work, a stable, green-coloured metallohydrogel was fabricated under ambient conditions through the spontaneous self-assembly of cobalt(II) nitrate hexahydrate, Co(NO3)2·6H2O, as the metal source with 3-amino-1-propanol acting as a low-molecular-weight gelator (LMWG) in aqueous medium. The synthesized metallogel was characterized using rheological analysis i.e.; strain sweep, frequency sweep and thixotropy. Surface morphology and network texture were probed by FESEM, elemental composition was verified by EDX analysis, and the gel's stimuli-responsive were subsequently evaluated.
items.authors: Tripti Dolai, Prity Chatterjee, Mallika Sharma, Suresh Kumar Yatirajula, Amiya Dey

items.title: Linear I···I contacts in a platinum(IV)-diiodo porphyrin: Emergent type III halogen–halogen interactions
items.abstract: This study presents experimental and theoretical evidence for unusual intermolecular I···I interactions between axially coordinated iodide ligands in a Pt(IV) porphyrin. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that PtI2T[3,5-diOMe]PP, where T[3,5-diOMe]PP is the 5,10,15,20-tetrakis(3,5-dimethoxyphenyl)porphyrinato dianion, crystallises in the uncommon P4/n space group, in contrast to the I4/m space group frequently observed for related metalloporphyrins, and adopts an eclipsed columnar packing arrangement, with co-crystallised dichloromethane (DCM) molecules occupying the space between successive porphyrin layers. The iodide ligands form linear I···I contacts that propagate into a one-dimensional supramolecular network. Comparison with the axial-iodide-free PtT[3,5-diOMe]PP and the related OsI2T[2,4,6-triMe]PP, where T[2,4,6-triMe]PP is the 5,10,15,20-tetrakis(2,4,6-trimethylphenyl)porphyrinato dianion, demonstrates how axial iodide coordination, peripheral substitution, and the local solvent environment influence the resulting crystal packing and macrocyclic conformation. Molecular surface electrostatic potential (MESP), quantum theory of atoms in molecules (QTAIM), natural bond orbital (NBO), and Hirshfeld surface analyses were employed to investigate the nature of the intermolecular contacts. QTAIM analysis identifies the I···I contacts as weak, closed-shell interactions, while NBO analysis reveals a significant donor–acceptor component involving iodide lone pairs and neighbouring Pt–I or Os–I antibonding orbitals. The magnitude and distribution of these interactions depend on the local supramolecular environment, with co-crystallised DCM contributing additional C–H···I contacts and altering the electronic environment of these ligands. Together, these results demonstrate that the I···I interactions cannot be considered in isolation, but instead form part of a broader network of cooperative intermolecular contacts that governs the crystal packing of the Pt(IV) porphyrin.
items.authors: Tristan K. Theunissen, Gerhard A. Venter, Catharine Esterhuysen, Abhik Ghosh, Susan A. Bourne

items.title: Addressing the nature and reductive stability of alkylthiol-modified Cu electrode surfaces
items.abstract: Cu surfaces modified with molecular adsorbates are being used in electrocatalyic processes (e.g., CO2 reduction (CO2RR)) to improve performance, but the nature and stability of molecular adsorbates (e.g. thiols) on Cu remain poorly understood owing to the sensitivity of Cu to oxidation and the complex chemical nature of the interface. To address these challenges, alkylthiol modification of 10 monolayers of electrodeposited Cu onto single-crystal Au bead electrodes has been prepared and studied using electrochemistry and in-situ fluorescence imaging. Under rigorous O2-free and H2O-free conditions, oxide-free Cu surfaces were produced. Modification of these oxide-free surfaces with alkylthiols resulted in a Cu2S overlayer. Oxide-free Cu surfaces modified with alkylthiol in the presence of trace H2O or O2 was found to have an increased amount of Cu2S, identified by electrochemistry and ex-situ Raman. The reductive stability of the alkylthiol modified Cu surface was investigated using a fluorophore-labelled DNA-alkylthiol adsorbate and in-situ fluorescence microscopy. Oxide-free Cu surfaces modified with alkylthiols produced a surface that was slightly more reductively stable (by-0.1 to-0.2V) when compared with alkylthiol self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) on Au, but do not show the characteristics of an alkyl-thiol SAM. Under similar modification procedures but using slightly oxidized Cu surfaces, the adsorbates were not removed using reducing potentials more negative than hydrogen evolution, suggesting a multilayer adsorbate structure composed of Cu2S with non-specifically adsorbed species. Thus, Cu surfaces prepared in the presence of trace O2and H2O may have a Cu-sulfide overlayer rather than a Cu-alkylthiol monolayer, even at reducing potentials typical of CO2RR or other electrocatalysis processes. More generally, the quantitative methodology that we developed for studying Cu electrodes is a framework for gaining insight into the preparation and molecular modification of other non-noble metal electrodes of interest for electrocatalysis.
items.authors: Daina V. Baker, Gilberto Martinez-Blanco, W. Russ Algar, Dan Bizzotto

items.title: Cuban Bentonite/Polymer Nanocomposites: A Sustainable Alternative for Food Packaging
items.abstract: The environmental impact of conventional polymers has driven the search for sustainable food packaging alternatives. Clay incorporation into polymers matrices has shown to enhance optical, mechanical, and barrier properties. This study evaluates Cuban natural bentonite as a reinforcing phase in hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC), carboxymethylcellulose (CMC), polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), and polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), plus their mixtures (PVA/PVP and PVA/CMC). Films were cast and characterized by XRD, ATR-FTIR, SEM, and water resistance tests; opacity was measured by UV-Vis spectroscopy accounting for thickness. Results indicate that polymer dispersion depends on temperature (CMC fastest). Bent/HPMC films stood out for their superior opacity and water resistance, while Bent/PVA/PVP and Bent/PVA/CMC showed predominantly exfoliated structures, favorable for food packaging applications.
items.authors: C. Leal, D. Hernández, M. Muñoz-Arias, E. Altshuler, A. Rivera

items.title: Counter-Intuitive Orthogonal Catalysis for In-Situ Functionalization of High-Performance Self-Blown Non-Isocyanate Polyurethane Foams
items.abstract: Rigid foams earn their place in structural applications through a specific balance of stiffness and density. Reproducing that balance without isocyanates has proven far harder than replacing the chemistry itself. Water-blown polyhydroxyurethane (PHU) foams are the most credible isocyanate-free alternatives to conventional polyurethanes, but toxic base catalysts and weak mechanical properties have stalled their adoption. Brønsted acid catalysis, long dismissed on the expectation that amine protonation suppresses urethane formation, proves effective instead: a dynamic equilibrium of transient protonation and thermal amine regeneration widens the rheological window for water-driven CO 2 release while carrying the network to full conversion. Acidic conditions additionally activate vinyl ethers, converting the pendant and vicinal hydroxyls responsible for moisture plasticization into acetal crosslinks. The resulting poly(hydroxyurethane)–polyacetal (PHU–PAC) foams show a sixteenfold (16x) higher rubbery modulus, a fourfold higher compressive modulus (4 → 18 MPa), and halved water uptake relative to the PHU benchmark. Normalized peak heat release rate falls nearly eightfold below that of a commercial PU foam, and on an Ashby plot of specific strength versus stiffness, PHU–PAC approaches HDPE and PVC. Addressing catalyst tractability, moisture uptake, and mechanical performance in one formulation, acid-catalyzed PHU–PAC reframes non-isocyanate foams as tunable structural materials and positions catalyst design as a lever for the next generation of sustainable cellular materials.
items.authors: Gabriel Perli, Guillem Seychal, Bruno A. Piscelli, Yi Wang, Maliheh Razavi-Esfali, Lucas Polo Fonseca

items.title: DeepEnzyKat: Turnover number prediction through enzyme-substrate interaction modeling and adaptive expert ensembles
items.authors: Guangran Zhang, Yujing Zhao, Yongwen Zhang, Yuhao Li, Ruihan Wang, Chengguang Bian

items.title: LANGER: Lanthanide Affinity Network via Graph and Evolutionary Representations
items.abstract: The transition to sustainable energy relies heavily on rare earth elements (REEs), yet their separation remains a critical industrial bottleneck due to their nearly identical physicochemical properties. The discovery of lanmodulin (LanM), a highly selective REE-binding protein, has inspired bio-based separation strategies; however, predicting binding affinity between different LanM variants and REEs remains a significant computational challenge. Here, we present LANGER, a multimodal deep learning framework for predicting REE protein binding affinity (Kd) by synchronously integrating global evolutionary context, continuous ionic chemistry, and local three-dimensional coordinate geometry. Our architecture combines ESM2 protein sequence embeddings, REE physicochemical descriptions, and geometric graph learning (GGL) features derived from topologies extracted from protein-ion complexes. Using a comprehensive dataset of 616 evaluated LanM homologs against 15 REE ions, we demonstrate the robustness of this framework across two rigorous evaluation settings. In a cluster-based validation analysis designed to test extrapolation to held-out LanM sequence clusters, LANGER achieved a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.212 and a concordance index (CI) of 0.757. More importantly, in a rigorous evaluation protocol that completely excludes individual ions from the training phase, the fully integrated multimodal framework achieved high predictive accuracy (RMSE = 0.119, Pearson correlation coefficient r = 0.860, CI = 0.800), demonstrating its unique ability to transfer learned physicochemical trends to unseen lanthanide elements. This work establishes a scalable, computationally accurate structure recognition platform for the discovery and design of data-driven REEselective proteins.
items.authors: Trung Nguyen, Christopher Cotter, Seunghyun Ryu, Cong T. Trinh, Duc Duy Nguyen

items.title: Direct Alkylarene Desaturation via Base-Promoted Halogen Transfer
items.abstract: We report a method to prepare alkenes through the base-promoted oxidative desaturation of alkylarenes and related weakly acidic functional groups. This process operates via a tandem deprotonative-halogenation and elimination sequence using haloarene halogen-transfer reagents. The use of potassium tert-butoxide with haloarene oxidants provides a simple means to desaturate a broad range of alkylarenes, acids, esters, and amides, as well as to aromatize saturated heterocycles. A critical feature for reaction success is the generation of tert-butanol from the tert-butoxide base which buffers the reaction solution to prevent anionic alkene polymerization. The utility of this approach is enhanced by its direct sequencing with additional base-promoted processes, such as hydrofunctionalization, to access formal homobenzylic C–H functionalization products.
items.authors: Eve L. Sugg, Garrett A. Hoteling, Viet Ngo, Jeffrey S. Bandar

items.title: Deciphering Charge-Transfer and Triplet-Multiplet Excited States in Substituted MnIII and CrIII Phthalocyanines: Insights from UV-Vis-NIR, MCD, and Theory
items.abstract: Charge-transfer (metal-to-ligand, MLCT, ligand-to-metal, LMCT, and interligand, (LLCT) and intraligand (π−π* and triplet-multiplet) transitions observed in the UV-vis-NIR and magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) spectra of high-spin Pc tBu Cr III Cl, Pc tBu Mn III Cl, and Pc OBu Mn III Cl (Pc tBu is the dianion of the 2,9(10),16(17),23(24)-tetra-tert-butyl-phthalocyanine and Pc OBu is the dianion of the 1,4,8,11,15,18,22,25-octa-n-butoxy-phthalocyanine) complexes were analyzed with the help of group theory combined with time-dependent density functional theory and ab initio (CASSCF and NEVPT2(13e,14o)) calculations. The energy shift between tert-butylated and butoxylated Pc rings, the energy shift between Mn and Cr centers, and the change in solvent donicity between dichloromethane/chloroform (DCM / CHCl 3 ) and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) were used to systematically perturb the energies of electronic transitions. It was demonstrated that the triplet-multiplet transitions dominate the NIR region of the UV-vis-NIR and MCD spectra, while LMCT bands dominate the “phthalocyanine window” (350-550 nm) region of the UV-vis-NIR and MCD spectra. Like other trivalent transition-metal phthalocyanines, MLCT transitions were predicted in the UV region of the UV-vis-NIR and MCD spectra. General trends in triplet-multiplet transitions across d 1 -d 9 configurations as well as the function of axial ligands for a given metal are delineated and parameterized. These studies will be used for further understanding of wavelength-dependent photochemical activity and the effects of structural substitutions on electrocatalytic and photocatalytic transformations.
items.authors: Kelsie J. Tuggle, Haleigh M. Grace, Breanna E. Muldowney, Ryan. S. Arnold, Emma E. Lane, Daniel B. Leznoff
items.title_zh: 解读取代MnIII和CrIII酞菁中的电荷转移及三重态多重态激发态
items.summary_zh: 本研究分析了高自旋Pc tBu Cr III Cl、Pc tBu Mn III Cl和Pc OBu Mn III Cl复合物的紫外-可见-近红外（UV-vis-NIR）和磁圆二色性（MCD）光谱中的电荷转移（金属-配体转移MLCT、配体-金属转移LMCT、配体间转移LLCT）及配体内转移（π−π*和三重态多重态）跃迁。通过结合群论、时间依赖密度泛函理论及从头算（CASSCF和NEVPT2(13e,14o)）计算，系统研究了取代基对电子跃迁能量的影响。结果表明，三重态多重态跃迁主导了UV-vis-NIR和MCD光谱的近红外区域，而LMCT带则主导了“酞菁窗口”（350-550 nm）区域。此外，预测了在紫外区域的MLCT跃迁，揭示了d 1 -d 9构型中三重态多重态跃迁的一般趋势。

items.title: Mechanistic regimes for electron transfer at bio–nano interfaces
items.abstract: Bioelectronic medicine increasingly operates at interfaces whose dimensions approach redox molecules, electrical double layers and structured electronic states. The central problem is therefore not to identify a size at which electrochemistry becomes quantum, but to determine which physical description explains a response. This challenge is acute for nanoscale bipolar electrodes, where conductor-scale potentials predicted from uniform-field models can be extremely small despite faradaic and biological activity. Local field concentration, double-layer overlap, ion-concentration polarisation, altered reorganisation energetics, stochastic molecular dynamics and electron tunnelling offer coexisting explanations. We propose a falsifiable framework that distinguishes continuum/device, interfacial/cellular, stochastic/few-molecule and quantum-informed regimes by perturbing local potential, field and length, molecular coupling, confinement and electronic structure. Quantum capacitance, bipolar electrochemistry, tunnelling junctions, activationless electron transfer and multiscale modelling illustrate these tests. Size determines when effects may become important; mechanism must be assigned from discriminating behaviour, not from size or endpoint response alone.
items.authors: Deepan Kumar Neethipathi, Frankie J. Rawson

items.title: Carbon dioxide expanded ionic liquid mixtures for changing reaction outcomes and efficient separation
items.authors: Aidan Jowett, Stuart Prescott, Raffaella Mammucari, Jason Harper

items.title: Rapid, High-Yielding, and Broad-Scope Silicon-Noded Single-Atom Ligation Platform
items.abstract: The node–module logic underpins DNA, RNA, and metal–organic frameworks. In small-molecule synthesis, SuFEx and PFEx exploit sulfur or phosphorus as single‑atom nodes for 10 modular ligations but are largely confined to amine and phenol modules. Silicon‑based ligation would offer a viable alternative, as both alcohols and phenols can serve as reliable modules, yet it has lacked efficient and controllable platforms. Herein, we report a silicon-noded ligation platform using bis(2,4,6-trimethoxyphenyl)silanes (bis(TMP)silanes) as the ligation hubs, enabling rapid, high-yielding ligation of both alcohol and phenol modules with broad functional-group tolerance.
items.authors: Jie Wang, Zhiyou Hu, Youliang Wang

items.title: Active control of crystal nucleation and growth using operando X-ray imaging
items.authors: Eslam M. Elbakry, Emma A. Pappas, Joshua C. Gibson, Daniel P. Shoemaker

items.title: Hierarchical Dimensionality Evolution of Ionic Transport in Superionic Copper Iodide
items.abstract: Superionic conductors exhibit liquid-like ion transport within a rigid solid framework enabled by dynamical sublattice decoupling. In copper iodide (CuI), fast ion conduction emerges through structural transitions that reshape the local energy landscape, yet the microscopic evolution of diffusion topology across phase transitions remains insufficiently understood. By integrating machine-learning Molecular Dynamics (MLMD) with lattice dynamics, we elucidate the temperature-dependent ionic transport mechanism in CuI. The superionic transition in CuI manifests as a hierarchical evolution of transport dimensionality, progressing sequentially from localized vibrations to 1D channel transport, 2D in-plane diffusion, and ultimately isotropic 3D migration. This hierarchical evolution is driven by transverse acoustic phonon softening, which modulates migration barriers through direction-selective geometric confinement via a triangular-gate regulation mechanism.
items.authors: Wenjie Yang, Jialin Liu, Fawei Tang, Zhaochuan Fan

items.title: Synthetic Mutagenesis of Tyrosine into Proline Mimetics Enables Late-Stage Backbone Editing of Peptides
items.abstract: The biological and physicochemical properties of peptides are strongly influenced by their backbone conformations. However, installing conformationally restricting units generally requires peptide redesign and resynthesis using noncanonical amino acids. Here, we report a late-stage backbone-editing method that converts a native amino acid residue into a proline-mimetic structure. Treatment of the dearomatized intermediate generated by tyrosine-selective oxime conjugation in a basic aqueous buffer induced intramolecular 1,4-addition of the backbone amide nitrogen, thereby converting the tyrosine residue into a cyclic proline-mimetic unit within the peptide backbone. This transformation proceeded efficiently under mild aqueous conditions and was applicable to several bioactive peptides. Multidimensional NMR analyses established the structures of the resulting products, while conventional molecular dynamics and REST2 simulations demonstrated that the installed proline-mimetic backbone reduced the local conformational freedom of the peptide. Evaluation using a β-hairpin model peptide further demonstrated that the proline-mimetic structure enhanced resistance to proteolytic degradation. This method constitutes a chemical mutagenesis strategy that directly converts a native tyrosine residue into a backbone conformational control unit without reconstructing the parent peptide sequence. By connecting residue-selective side-chain modification with backbone editing, this strategy provides a new design concept for the late-stage conformational and functional diversification of peptides.
items.authors: Takaya Togo, Takumi Ueda, Yuko Otani, Yuka Furukawa, Kohei Nogita, Katsuya Maruyama

items.title: Computational investigation of the first most (𝝅; 𝝅∗)𝟏; (𝒏; 𝝅∗)𝟏;(𝝅; 𝝈∗)𝟏 and (𝒏; 𝝈∗)𝟏 electronic states of all possible positional isomers of iodinated BODIPY
items.abstract: Photochemistry of all possible positional isomers of iodinated -BODIPY has been explored employing state of the art two-component relativistic sf-X2C-S-TD-DFT-SOC method. Vertical excitation energies; oscillator strength and spin–orbit couplings of first most promising electronic states have been computed. Effect of number of iodine atoms attached to BODIPY moiety and their topology on magnitude of vertical excitation energies have been explained in detail. Slater–Condon rules and El–Sayed rules which are special case of former have been effectively employed to explain magnitude of spin–orbit couplings between states of different multiplicities. Coupled states exhibiting anomalies from conventional El–Sayed rules have been explained with the help of orbitals involved in respective states. Effect of non-planarity of BODIPY ring on magnitude of spin–orbit couplings between states of different multiplicities have also been discussed. Most effective positions on BODIPY moiety that can turn in to effective photosensitizer by attaching iodine atoms on them has been explored and explained.
items.authors: Maria Hasan, Jakub Višňák, Tashfeen Akhtar, Mirza Wasif Baig

items.title: An open implementation of MSEVB for reactive force field simulation with simple energy-based coupling
items.abstract: Chemical reactivity modelling in large systems over extended timescales is computationally and theoretically challenging; ab initio methods are too expensive, while classical force fields cannot handle bond breaking/formation. Existing solutions like reactive force fields require extensive expertise to develop, and machine-learned approaches often need prohibitively large, high-quality datasets for training. These barriers have hindered the modelling of reactive chemical processes. Multi-state empirical valence bond (MSEVB) theory offers an alternative by enabling conventional unreactive force fields to be mixed in a controlled manner to selectively describe chemical reactions. However, existing MSEVB implementations are often field-specific, have license-restricted distribution, or rely on complex parameterisation schemes. This work presents a new open-source, general MSEVB implementation, designed to make reactive modelling more accessible to non-experts. Specifically, the implementation here focused on simple energy-based coupling, thereby eliminating the need for complex geometry-based coupling approaches, significantly lowering the barrier to entry for reactive force field development. This generalised approach is demonstrated to reproduce proton transfer behaviour in Y-doped and undoped BaZrO3, bulk water and liquid imidazole, as well as other forms of reactivity, such as electron migration in LiCoO2. We demonstrate that only two fitted parameters are needed to accurately model symmetric transfer across the three chemically diverse proton-conducting systems studied
items.authors: Blake I. Armstrong, Peter R. Spackman, Luc M. LeBlanc, Paolo Raiteri, Julian D. Gale

items.title: Preclinical and Pilot Human Evaluation of [18F]NIDF-1, an N-Protonation-Guided Tau PET Tracer
items.abstract: Hyperphosphorylated tau aggregates are a pathological hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and an important target for positron emission tomography (PET) imaging. Guided by the hypothesis that N-protonation enables electrostatic interactions with negatively charged sites associated with tau hyperphosphorylation, we designed and synthesized a focused series of azaindole derivatives and identified NIDF-1 as a lead compound by competitive autoradiography on AD brain sections (IC50 = 22.1 ± 6.8 nM). NIDF-1 showed low amyloid-β (Aβ) cross-reactivity and limited off-target toward monoamine oxidases (MAO). [18F]NIDF-1 exhibited favorable brain kinetics in rodents, with an initial brain uptake of 7.57% ID/g in mice and a peak brain mean standardized uptake value (SUVmean) of 2.20 in Sprague–Dawley (SD) rats, followed by rapid clearance (2-to-60-min brain uptake ratios of 18.46 and 3.30, respectively). Autoradiography confirmed preferential binding to ADassociated tau pathology. In a pilot human PET study, [18F]NIDF-1 showed higher cortical retention in an AD participant than in a healthy control. These findings identify [18F]NIDF-1 as a promising tau PET tracer with favorable tau binding affinity, brain kinetics, and encouraging initial human imaging results, while supporting N-protonation as a useful design consideration for tau-targeted imaging agents. KEYWORDS: N-Protonation, Tau PET tracer, Azaindole, Alzheimer’s disease
items.authors: Wantong Guo, Yishuo Wang, Yuying Li, Xiaojun Zhang, Nan Wu, Qilei Zhang

items.title: Sensitized near-infrared luminescence in sulfur-coordinated lanthanide complexes for machine learning-enhanced thermometry
items.abstract: Lanthanide (Ln 3+ ) coordination complexes featuring only Ln–S bonds have optical properties uniquely modulated by soft donor atoms. Yet, these complexes and their applications are underexplored, due to the stricter environmental control required for their typical preparation relative to complexes containing Ln–O bonds. Herein, we show that Ln-S coordination is ideally suited to generate information-rich near-infrared (NIR) photoluminescence, laying the optimal ground for machine learning-driven optical sensing. We prepared three new homoleptic complexes with general formula [K(2.2.2-cryptand)][Ln( L ) 4 ] (Ln = Nd 3+ ( 1-Nd ), Gd 3+ ( 1-Gd ), or Yb 3+ ( 1-Yb ); L = 2,6-bis-(4- tert -butylphenyl)phenyldithiocarboxylate). In all complexes, the Ln 3+ ion is dodecahedrally coordinated to eight sulfur atoms, generating a crystal field that deviates from the ideal anisotropic case and leads to substantial mixing of the crystal-field states, as revealed by magnetic measurements and ab initio calculations. Temperature-dependent photoluminescence and optical absorption measurements allowed identifying the electronic transitions and energy transfer mechanisms underpinning the complexes’ optical properties, which are dominated by ligand sensitization of the Ln 3+ emission. Survey of the photoluminescence-vs-temperature (calibration) datasets indicated the amenability of 1-Nd and 1-Yb to luminescence thermometry. Chiefly, the complex spectral variations induced by thermal changes can be comprehensively analyzed via principal component analysis, thus extracting global optical features with readout precision that is one order of magnitude higher than classical, local spectral features. More broadly, this study demonstrates that spectral complexity in molecular systems sets the necessary preconditions for advanced optical sensing supported by machine learning algorithms.
items.authors: Mikko Rautiainen, Emily Andreato, Essi Barkas, Liyan Ming, Nikita Panov, Hannu Huhtinen

items.title: When Is a Molecule a Duplicate? Identity Policy Determines What a Benchmark Audit Finds
items.abstract: Reports of duplicate or redundant records in molecular machine-learning benchmarks are routinely presented as properties of the datasets. They are not. A duplicate count is the output of an operational definition of molecular identity applied to a dataset, and different defensible definitions return different answers from the same file. We audited seven MoleculeNet [3] benchmarks (52,144 records) under a four-level identity hierarchy — canonical molecular graph, fragment parent, charge-normalised parent and tautomer-normalised parent — with the Standard InChIKey as an orthogonal comparator rather than a rung, and with derived identity withheld outside a declared domain of applicability. Duplicate-group counts moved with the level in every benchmark, and for three the audit changed its answer to whether the benchmark contains duplicate compounds at all. Domain choice mattered as much: HIV reports 330 duplicate groups at the tautomer-normalised level when identity is asserted for every record, against 124 on the declared domain. A post hoc sensitivity analysis found that domain under-covered main-group and f-block metal-associated structures, giving 109 without displacing 124 as the prespecified result. Of 295 merge events, 179 were decidable from structure alone and 116 were policy-dependent; across that complete census, 19 events (16.4%; 41 records) received a different benchmark-equivalence decision from transition-appropriate official-InChI arbitration under an endpoint rulebook fixed before final classification, all 19 in one benchmark's stereochemical subset. We publish the identity policy as an executable, fingerprinted contract reproducing every reported count exactly (434/434), so the assumptions behind an audit statistic can be inspected and re-executed rather than inferred.
items.authors: Md. Rahul Reza Roktim

items.title: Water Layering and Orientation Modulate Lanthanide Hydration in Carbon Nanotubes
items.abstract: Nanoscale confinement can reorganize water molecules and alter ionic hydration, offering a potential route to separating chemically similar ions. We use molecular dynamics simulations with the MACE-MH-1 foundation machine-learning interatomic potential to investigate the hydration of eight trivalent lanthanide ions (Ln 3+ : La 3+ , Pr 3+ , Nd 3+ , Gd 3+ , Tb 3+ , Dy 3+ , Tm 3+ , and Lu 3+ ) in carbon nanotubes (CNTs) with diameters of 1.09–1.49 nm. We first evaluate MACE-MH-1 for Ln 3+ hydration in bulk solution. The OMOL model of MACE-MH-1 reproduces the reported Ln–O distances and coordination-number trends and is therefore used for the CNT simulations. The hydration factor, which measures first-shell orientational order, varies nonmonotonically with CNT diameter and reaches a minimum in CNT(9,9), which also accommodates the most first-shell water molecules. This minimum coincides with the emergence of a central water population and reflects two combined effects: difference in preferred orientation between first-shell and surrounding water molecules and increased hydrogen-bond coupling between them. However, different Ln 3+ ions respond similarly to confinement, suggesting that CNT confinement alone may offer limited selectivity for their separation.
items.authors: Kailong Zhang, Jian Shi, Qing Shao

items.title: CO2 Electrosorption: Electric Field Effect on the Metal–CO2 Interfacial Dipole
items.abstract: CO2 electrosorption at metal electrodes is a critical step controlling the subsequent electrochemical reduction process, yet its physicochemical origin remains debated. The field-induced stabilization of adsorbed CO2 – the field effect − is commonly attributed to the interaction between the applied electric field and the adsorption-induced molecular dipole of CO2 . In this study, we employ density functional theory with an applied electric field to re-examine this paradigm by studying CO2 electrosorption on (111) surfaces of Ag, Au, Cu, Ir, Pb, and Pt. We show an electric-field-driven transition between physisorbed and chemisorbed CO2 . Physisorption preserves a near-linear geometry with negligible charge transfer and weak field dependence, whereas chemisorption involves pronounced bending and substantial electron transfer from the metal. Collectively, we demonstrate that the field effect arises from the interaction between the electric field and the interfacial metal–CO2 dipole formed upon charge transfer, rather than the molecular CO2 dipole alone, as conventionally assumed.
items.authors: Anna Stepanova, Ba Long Nguyen, Nadezda Kongi, Vladislav Ivanistsev

items.title: Coordinate bonding, cluster delocalization and topological criticality in a cyclic trimeric beryllium–dinitrogen complex
items.abstract: Fixation and coordination of molecular dinitrogen (N2) by main-group clusters offer fundamental insight into non-classical multi-centre bonding and light-metal activation pathways. Here we report a combined density-functional and ab initio study of the cyclic cluster Be3(N2)3. Geometry optimization and frequency analysis establish a stable, closed-shell Cs-symmetric trimer containing an isosceles triangular Be3 metal core coordinated end-on by three terminal N2 ligands. Energy decomposition analysis coupled with natural orbitals for chemical valence (ETS-NOCV) shows that the Be3⋯(N2)3 interaction is dominated by orbital contributions (≈60 % of attractive forces), supplemented by electrostatic attraction that together overcome Pauli repulsion. Quantum theory of atoms in molecules (QTAIM) identifies two non-nuclear attractors along the apical–basal Be–Be edges, while electron localization function (ELF) and localized orbital locator (LOL) basin analyses reveal a distinct heart-shaped trisynaptic valence basin V(Be,Be,Be) populated by ≈1.8–2.0 electrons. These topological signatures establish multi-centre σ-aromatic delocalization as the structural foundation of the central metallacycle and demonstrate that light alkaline-earth elements can support non-classical N2 coordination frameworks.
items.authors: D K Jha, M Pathak, Dhananjay Kumar Jha

items.title: Sampling Budget as a Confound in Dimensionality-Reduction Analyses of Molecular Simulation
items.abstract: A common claim in molecular simulation is that projecting a trajectory reveals N metastable states. Here N is operationally the number of Gaussian-mixture components selected in a low-dimensional embedding, without a kinetic model it should be read as an apparent-basin count, not a validated metastable-state count. Across two potentials with basin counts fixed by construction and two independent 100 ns alanine-dipeptide simulations, the BIC-selected component count rises strongly with sampling budget (Spearman rho = 0.87-0.97 across systems and methods) although the reference landscape is unchanged. The trend persists under uniform thinning of a common reference trajectory, where coverage is approximately matched, and under IID Boltzmann sampling in the exact synthetic latent coordinates, which removes time correlation and projection learning. Other criteria exhibit different failure modes: AIC is frequently ceiling-censored or non-monotone, ICL never reaches the tested ceiling but remains method-dependently inaccurate, and silhouette and the simple elbow diagnostic are largely insensitive. BIC-selected recovery often peaks at an intermediate budget and then declines even while recovery at the reference component count is flat or improves. One exception is explicit, alanine TICA seed 1 shows no decline within the tested range because its high-recovery crossover occurs at the last budget. We recommend reporting sampling-budget curves, treating mixture components as candidate states until kinetically validated, and using ICL only as a less-ceiling-prone sensitivity analysis rather than a general default.
items.authors: Jaiveer Bassi

items.title: Self-Salting Coacervates: Interfacial Tension Reveals a Critical-Like Self-Suppression of Complex Coacervation
items.abstract: Complex coacervation, the associative liquid\liquid phase separation of oppositely charged polyelectrolytes, is a widely used physicochemical model for the principles underlying biomolecular condensates and for applications in encapsulation and underwater adhesion. Coacervation is typically controlled through the ionic strength of an added salt, while the role of polyelectrolyte concentration itself has received much less attention. Here we show that increasing polymer concentration can itself progressively suppress complex coacervation in a charge-stoichiometric, salt-free poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride)/sodium polyacrylate system. As the polymer concentration increases, the coacervate phase swells while the fraction of polymer recovered in it stays nearly constant, and the compositions and densities of the coacervate and supernatant phases progressively converge. At a polymer concentration of 400 mM, the macroscopic phase boundary vanishes and the system reaches a homogeneous, self-suppressed coacervation state. Over this range, the liquid\liquid interfacial tension decreases continuously toward zero, following a critical-like power law with an exponent of 1.43±0.03, close to the classical mean-field value of 3/2. These results show that polyelectrolyte concentration is not merely a compositional variable but can itself drive coacervation toward a critical-like, homogeneous state by increasing salt-like screening from polymer-derived counterions, analogous to the effect of added salt.
items.authors: Yue Yu, Hongwei Li, Christophe Schatz, Jean-Paul Chapel

items.title: In-Situ and Label-Free Quantification of BSA Adsorption on Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles via Orthogonal Analysis in Analytical Ultracentrifugation
items.abstract: Understanding the bio–nano interface requires precise, in-situ and label-free tools to characterize the protein corona. While hydrodynamic techniques like dynamic light scattering (DLS) and nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA) are widely used, they face inherent limitations: DLS provides ensemble-averaged signals and often requires specific optical models, whereas NTA’s temporal resolution limits its accuracy for ultra-small particles. Here, we demonstrate the power of custom-built multiwavelength analytical ultracentrifugation (MWL-AUC) as a superior orthogonal platform to characterize the bovine serum albumin (BSA) corona on mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs). By integrating three independent analytical dimensions, i.e. in-situ supernatant depletion, density-based sedimentation analysis, and multiwavelength spectral decoupling, we achieved precise quantification of both the total adsorbed BSA and its spatial distribution. This approach enables a quantitative mapping of protein localization that transcends mere qualitative observations of aggregation. Specifically, we show that the compositional information from spectral decoupling provides a robust cross-validation for the effective density analysis, which fundamentally dictates the precision of the derived spatial distribution. This study establishes a self-validating framework for the precise characterization of protein corona on porous nanostructures, offering vital insights for the rational design of nanocarriers in complex biological environments.
items.authors: Chao Zhang, Mengdi Chen, Bingwen Hu, E Wu

items.title: MaRs: A Universal Python Library for Steady-State and Time-Resolved EPR Simulations
items.abstract: MaRs is an open-source Python library for the simulation and fitting of electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra. MaRs supports simulations of field-swept and frequency-swept continuous-wave EPR, accounting for various spin-sublevel polarizations. Moreover, MaRs is capable of simulating complete 2D time-resolved EPR spectra (in field-time domain). The latter can be computed in different levels of theoretical complexity. First, the time evolution can be computed either with kinetic rate equations, which describe population transfer, or in full Liouville space, which captures coherence dynamics. Second, the relaxation pathways in timeresolved simulations can be specified either through intuitive rate parameters that are automatically expanded into the Lindblad master-equation form, or derived microscopically using the Bloch-Redfield formalism. To handle physically complex relaxation scenarios, MaRs provides automatic thermal-balance enforcement and composition operations that allow multicomponent relaxation models to be assembled from simple building blocks. Built on PyTorch (popular platform for machine learning development), MaRs leverages operations on both CPU and CUDA (GPU) backends. We demonstrate MaRs time-resolved EPR capabilities as well the differences and limitations of each built-in approach to time-domain simulations on the examples of coupled triplet-doublet pairs and systems exhibiting the reverse intersystem crossing phenomenon. Separately, we validate stationary EPR simulations across diverse spin systems, including high-spin complexes, achieving excellent agreement with established packages. We also show the possibilities of parameter fitting framework, applicable to all spectrum types implemented in MaRs, that supports multiple optimization strategies and uncertainty quantification.
items.authors: Arkady Samsonenko, Ivan Kurganskii, Alexander Maryasov, Sergey Veber, Matvey Fedin

items.title: Enhancement of Sensory Hop Aroma by Extending the Whirlpool Settling Time
items.authors: Toru KISHIMOTO

items.title: Dynamic Coordination Enables Moisture-Tolerant Organoaluminum Catalysis for Controlled Ring-Opening Polymerization
items.abstract: Reconciling high catalytic activity with air/moisture stability remains a fundamental challenge in the development of efficient organometallic catalysts for the ring‑opening polymerization (ROP). In this contribution, we present a dynamic Lewis-base coordination strategy that regulates the coordination environment of an organoaluminum catalyst to balance these competing requirements. A structurally simple organoaluminum catalyst featuring a dynamic THF ligand, MeAl(BHT)2(THF) (BHT = 2,6-di-tert-butyl-4-methylphenoxy), is easily prepared from commercially available trimethylaluminum, 2,6-di-tert-butyl-4-methylphenol and tetrahydrofuran (THF) without tedious purification. In contrast to the parent MeAl(BHT)2, MeAl(BHT)2(THF) exhibits substantially enhanced air/moisture tolerance while retaining good catalytic activity and controllability toward the ROP of a diversity of lactones and lactide. Notably, MeAl(BHT)2(THF) enable controlled ROP of commercially as-received monomers without prior drying or purification. In particular, MeAl(BHT)2(THF) achieves a high turnover frequency (TOF) of 8400 h-1 for the bulk ROP of l-lactide conducted at 180 °C in air. The single-crystal structural analysis and in-situ NMR experiments collaboratively confirm the dynamic coordination and dissociation of the THF ligand, which accounts for the balance of high activity and moisture tolerance. This dynamic ligand strategy affords a robust organometallic catalyst with facile preparation, good activity and ambient stability, facilitating practical scalable aliphatic polyester synthesis.
items.authors: Qin Yan, Pingtao Ge, Shuyi Wang, Yong Shen, Zhibo Li

items.title: Closed-loop optimization in an industrial R D lab
items.abstract: In industrial research and development, autonomous closed-loop reaction optimizers have the potential to significantly accelerate processes, but they must be robust and flexible, encompassing both hardware and software components. This paper presents a versatile system developed and deployed within a research unit of an industrial R D lab, designed to address a variety of industry-relevant challenges rather than functioning as a one-off demonstrator. Unlike traditional systems that may focus on specific chemical processes, our approach facilitates the optimization of reactions across multiple organic synthesis research groups. We illustrate the system’s capabilities through three case studies, showcasing its adaptability and effectiveness in real-world applications. By prioritizing configurability and reusability, this work aims to contribute to a more sustainable and efficient approach to chemical engineering practices in industrial settings where interdisciplinary collaboration is key.
items.authors: Behrang Shafei, Robert Lee, Steffen Hoecker, Matthias Schmalzbauer, Bernd Schaefer

items.title: Tokenising quantum data for label-efficient training of molecular models
items.abstract: A model of molecular energies is limited by how much reference data can be afforded, because every training example is itself an expensive calculation. The practical question is therefore not “how accurate can this get” but “how much accuracy do I get per labelled molecule.” We built a representation of a molecule’s quantum features, which we call a quantum token and which a model consumes alongside whatever representation it already uses. The energy of a molecule in a given orbital basis is a linear functional of its one-and two-particle reduced density matrices, so those matrices, rather than the atomic coordinates, are the object the answer is actually computed from. A cheap calculation already produces an approximate one, and the token is a fixed-length encoding of it. It is not a token in the language-model sense: it is a vector of real numbers, not a discrete symbol drawn from a vocabulary, and the name refers to a unit of quantum information minted once and reused by many downstream models. No quantum hardware is involved: an ordinary classical model is trained on these features to predict the residual of the cheap calculation, the part a fast method gets wrong. Only the features are quantum. Holding the learner, the scaffold-disjoint split and the training-set size fixed and varying only the input features, adding the token to a production descriptor makes it 4.4–5.3× more accurate at equal training data, and a model given 50 labelled molecules is more accurate than the same model given 16,000 without it. At 20 to 52 heavy atoms, the size of drug candidates and the range where these models are applied in drug discovery rather than on public benchmarks, 93.7% of molecules fall within chemical accuracy, against 65.0% for the strongest classical descriptor and 4.4% for the uncorrected cheap method.
items.authors: Derya Karli

items.title: Growth and Postsynthetic Modulation of Morphology-Encoded Plasmonic Chirality
items.abstract: Establishing how nanoscale morphology gives rise to plasmonic chirality requires understanding both its development during nanoparticle growth and its response to subsequent structural modification. Here, we investigate these complementary processes within a single nanoparticle platform through cysteine-directed Au growth followed by Ag overgrowth. Initially achiral Au bipyramids evolve into irregular, faceted nanoparticles displaying strong bisignate circular dichroism (CD), with L- and D-cysteine producing approximately mirror-related responses. Varying the relative proportions of the cysteine enantiomers systematically controls the sign and magnitude of the CD response, with near cancellation for the racemic mixture. Time-resolved measurements reveal that the positive and negative CD bands develop with comparable sigmoidal Avrami-type kinetics, quantitatively capturing the emergence of plasmonic chirality during growth. Once chirality is established, subsequent Ag deposition without additional cysteine progressively blue-shifts the plasmonic response and attenuates the CD of both enantiomeric nanoparticles without sign reversal. This attenuation accompanies the transformation of the irregular, faceted Au exterior into a smoother and more rounded Ag-rich outer morphology. Together, these observations connect the emergence and postsynthetic attenuation of plasmonic chirality and highlight the importance of the asymmetric nanoparticle exterior in sustaining morphology-encoded chiroptical activity.
items.authors: Shubhangi Sharma, Susmita Pradhan, Arun Pratap Singh, Satyajit Patra

items.title: Fully bio-based precursor for photocurable networks: synthesis and photopolymerization of furan-vegetable oil derivative
items.abstract: The development of fully bio-based photocurable resins represents a promising sustainable alternative to conventional petroleum-derived materials. In this study, novel furan-based macromonomers were synthesized via a two-step synthetic route. The first step involved the transesterification of dimethyl 2,5-furandicarboxylate (DMFDCA) with dilinoleic diol (DD) using various catalysts, followed by methacrylation with methacryloyl chloride to introduce terminal vinyl functionalities. The chemical structures of the intermediates and final macromonomers were confirmed by 1 H NMR and FT-IR spectroscopy. Rheological characterization was conducted to evaluate flow behavior and processability. Thermal properties and phase behavior were investigated by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), revealing an amorphous and flexible polymer architecture with thermally induced crosslinking at elevated temperatures. Photopolymerization kinetics were analyzed using photo-DSC with different type-I photoinitiators under controlled UV irradiation conditions, while network formation was further evaluated through gel fraction analysis of photocured samples prepared under ambient conditions. Additionally, cytocompatibility studies were performed to assess the potential suitability of the materials for biomedical applications. Overall, this systematic investigation provides valuable insights into the design and synthesis of renewable, photocurable furan-based materials for advanced biomedical applications and sustainable manufacturing.
items.authors: Amna Sadiq, Agata Goszczyńska, Miroslawa El Fray

items.title: Biosynthetic Plausibility Mapper: Reaction-Aware Prioritization of Plant Metabolite Candidates Using Curated Pathway Context
items.abstract: Untargeted plant metabolomics can generate numerous structurally plausible annotations and candidate structures, but structural similarity alone does not establish whether a compound is consistent with the biosynthetic context represented by the detected metabolome. Integrating curated biochemical relationships with chemical similarity could therefore provide an additional, interpretable layer for candidate prioritization. Here, we present Biosynthetic Plausibility Mapper (BPM), an opensource cheminformatics application that maps user-provided plant metabolite annotations onto a locally constructed PlantCyc-derived knowledge base and explicitly distinguishes detected compounds, curated pathway context, and computationally prioritized candidates. BPM integrates chemical-identity reconciliation, curated reaction and pathway relationships, structural similarity, and global-context coherence into a decomposable candidate-ranking framework. In pathway-based benchmarking against hard structural decoys, BPM v3.1 achieved AUROC and AUPRC values of 1.000 and ranked the reference compound first in all 20 trials. In a more stringent adversarial benchmark containing biosynthetically plausible alternatives, v3.1 improved AUROC from 0.920 to 0.985, AUPRC from 0.574 Biosynthetic Plausibility Mapper to 0.837, and Top-1 accuracy from 65% to 90% relative to v3. A compact phenylpropanoid–flavonoid example illustrates the separation of experimental annotations, curated context, and prioritized hypotheses, while a larger Arabidopsis occurrence dataset demonstrates application to 864 mapped compounds within a 6,714-node network. BPM therefore provides an interpretable framework for converting annotated plant metabolite lists into ranked biosynthetic hypotheses without conflating computational plausibility with compound identification. By combining curated biochemical context with structural evidence and exporting prioritized candidates for targeted interrogation of LC–MS/MS data, BPM provides a practical link between metabolite annotation, biosynthetic interpretation, and subsequent experimental investigation.
items.authors: Lucas Jesus Patrício, Rômulo Pereira de Jesus, Ísis Tavares Vilas Boas, Fernanda Oliveira Chagas, Ricardo Moreira Borges

items.title: MPID Polarizable Force Field: GPU Implementation and Biomolecular Simulations
items.abstract: The multipole and induced dipole (MPID) model provides a sophisticated description of electrostatics through permanent atomic multipoles up to the octopole level and point induced dipoles, but its high computational cost has limited its routine application to biomolecular simulations. Here, we present a GPU-accelerated implementation of the MPID model in OpenMM. The implementation produces energies and forces fully consistent with those obtained from CHARMM and enables routine microsecond-scale molecular dynamics simulations of explicitly solvated protein systems. Moreover, force field parameters were transferred directly from the Drude oscillator model to the MPID framework without reparameterization, yielding the MPID-2019 protein force field. Tests on five proteins show that MPID-2019 reproduces a range of NMR observables, including scalar couplings and relaxation order parameters. These results demonstrate that MPID-2019 is a valid polarizable force field readily applicable to protein simulations and that the effective equivalence of the induced dipole and Drude oscillator formalisms can be established at the biomolecular level.
items.authors: Qiaozhu Tan, Andrew C Simmonett, Bernard R. Brooks, Jing Huang

items.title: Operational insights from the front lines of OpenADMET: lessons from our blind challenges
items.abstract: The gap between reported machine learning (ML) model performance in drug discovery and the experience of using these models in live discovery projects remains a major hurdle for the field, because the retrospective nature of most benchmarks makes it difficult to objectively assess progress. To address this gap, OpenADMET has hosted a series of blind challenges to benchmark and advance predictive modeling in absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET). In this Perspective, we distill the operational, strategic, and community-level lessons from our first four blind challenges, providing a practical blueprint for designing and running collaborative machine learning competitions in the life sciences. In addition, we open-source our blind challenge infrastructure and data-validation tools to lower the barrier to entry for hosting rigorous, community-driven competitions and to foster a sustainable framework for collective learning in computer-aided drug discovery.
items.authors: Hugo MacDermott-Opeskin, Maria Castellanos, Jonathan A. Swain, Jenke Scheen, Sean Colby, Georgia Channing

items.title: SimSJSAlert: A Similarity-Augmented Multi-View Learning Framework with Scaffold Alerts for Drug-Induced Stevens-Johnson Syndrome Risk Assessment
items.abstract: Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) is a rare, life-threatening adverse drug reaction for which early identification of high-risk drugs remains challenging. In this study, we developed an explainable quantitative structure-toxicity relationship (QSTR) framework for SJS prediction using a multi-view learning framework with 21 molecular representations, including molecular descriptors, fingerprints, transformer-based embeddings, and a molecular similarity representation. Model development and evaluation were designed in accordance with the OECD principles for QSAR validation, incorporating scaffold-aware validation, external evaluation on pharmacovigilance negative-signal compounds, and structural interpretation by integrating SHAP with Bemis-Murcko scaffold enrichment analysis. The proposed framework achieved robust sensitivity and specificity, with molecular similarity consistently improving the identification of SJS-associated compounds. Furthermore, a consensus prediction and scaffold-based prioritization strategy identified several high-risk drugs from the 1 external negative-signal dataset, including cefprozil, tetracycline, and omadacycline, highlighting their potential association with SJS and warranting further pharmacovigilance and experimental investigation. To facilitate practical application, this was deployed as a freely accessible web server, SimSJSAlert (https: //sim-sjs-alert.streamlit.app/), enabling rapid drug-induced SJS risk assessment. The proposed framework combines predictive performance, interpretability, and accessibility to support early SJS risk assessment, pharmacovigilance signal prioritization, and safer drug development.
items.authors: Huynh Anh Duy, Sastiya Kampaengsri, Supreeya Paiboon, Tarapong Srisongkram

items.title: Thermodynamics-Driven Treatability Investigation of Energy-Storage-Related Emerging PFAS
items.abstract: Bis-perfluoroalkyl sulfonimides (bis-FASIs), widely used in lithium-ion battery electrolytes, are increasingly detected in the environment, yet their transformation and treatability remain poorly understood. Here, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were integrated with experiments to determine how molecular structure controls bis-FASIs degradation. During electrochemical oxidation (EO) and UV/sulfite (UV/S) treatment, degradation and defluorination generally increased with perfluoroalkyl-chain length, with bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide (bis-FMeSI) being the most recalcitrant homolog. Although both processes nearly completely transformed bis-FMeSI, its fluorine fate differed markedly. EO produced trifluoromethanesulfonate (TFMS) at nearly stoichiometric yield, whereas UV/S generated both TFMS and trifluoromethanesulfonamide (TfNH 2 ). Marcus-theory calculations established the redox thresholds for one-electron transfer, while electronic-structure analysis showed that oxidation and reduction generate distinct states that follow different bond-cleavage pathways. Further transformation of TFMS and TfNH 2 required redox conditions beyond those attainable within the aqueous-phase stability window, causing their accumulation and limiting defluorination. To overcome this constraint, we demonstrated a cross-media approach in which bis-FMeSI and TFMS were adsorbed from water onto granular activated carbon and subsequently destroyed by additive-free ball milling with stainless-steel media, achieving complete degradation and near-quantitative recovery of organofluorine as fluoride. This cross-media strategy provides a potential solution for PFAS resistant to aqueous-phase treatment.
items.authors: Xiaotian Xu, Jinyuan Zhu, Yunqiao Guan, Yang Yang

items.title: From Rim to Core: Nitrile Coordination Creates an Electronic Gradient across Cu12 Nanocluster Nodes for CO2-to-Formate Electrosynthesis
items.abstract: Atomically precise copper nanoclusters offer an opportunity to program catalysis across individual metal positions, yet reticulation has largely been used to stabilize clusters rather than differentiate them electronically. Here, nitrile coordination converts a Cu12S9 nanocluster node into a radially polarized catalytic ensemble in Cu12TPN MOF. Single-crystal analysis resolves a thiolate-supported Cu12 architecture whose four terephthalonitrile linkers selectively address peripheral Cu sites. Bader analysis reveals an electronic gradient from electron-deficient nitrile-bound rim sites (~+0.57 |e|) to an electron-rich Cu–S/Cu interior (~+0.32–0.37 |e|). This coordination-encoded asymmetry translates directly into CO2 reduction, delivering 63.32% Faradaic efficiency for HCOOH with negligible CO formation. Density functional theory identifies a 0.91 eV energetic separation favoring O-bound *OCOH over *COOH at the pathway bifurcation, while H adsorption remains unfavorable. Post-electrolysis spectroscopy confirms persistence of the cluster-derived environment. These results establish reticulation as an electronic programming strategy within, rather than merely around, atomically precise nanocluster nodes. Atomically precise metal nanoclusters (NCs) occupy an unusual catalytic regime in which composition, metalmetal connectivity, ligand coordination, and individual surface sites can all be resolved at the atomic level.1-24 Unlike nanoparticles with distributed surface sites, NCs provide finite multinuclear ensembles in which structural and electronic perturbations can be traced from specific coordination events to catalytic consequences. Copper nanoclusters are especially attractive in this regard because the adaptable coordination chemistry of Cu(I), flexible Cu–S bonding, and short Cu···Cu contacts permit substantial redistribution of geometry and electron density within a single cluster.25-42 Yet this same adaptability makes it difficult to preserve atomically defined Cu ensembles under catalytic conditions.
items.authors: Sreelakshmi, Tsukasa Irie, Tokuhisa Kawawaki, Milan Kumar Jena, Saikat Das, Yuichi Negishi

items.title: Chemical synthesis of an atomically precise 2.5-MDa protein capsid and its mirror image
items.abstract: Protein capsids perform a broad range of biological functions 1–4 and can be engineered 5 as delivery vehicles, 6 nanoreactors, 7 biosensors, 8 and vaccines. 9 However, because the protein building blocks that make up these capsids must be expressed in biological systems, their composition is largely restricted to the canonical amino acids, limiting functionality. Assembling capsids from chemically synthesized proteins could circumvent this limitation but has not been accomplished due to a combination of technical challenges. Here we demonstrate the complete chemical synthesis of the 14.1-kDa coat protein of bacteriophage Qβ and its assembly into 180-subunit 2.5-MDa capsids. We exploit the expanded chemical palette afforded by total synthesis to produce mirror-image capsids composed entirely of unnatural D-amino acids. We determine the structures of the L- and D-capsids to 3-Å resolution by cryo-EM and verify their stereochemistry by cryo-ET. D-capsids elicit antibody titers 100-fold lower than their L-counterparts in mice, with the D-capsid response dominated by IgM antibodies. We demonstrate functional delivery in vivo using synthetic L-and D-capsids loaded with luciferase-encoding mRNA. By combining biological self-assembly with chemical synthesis, our results establish a route to producing a new class of programmable nanomaterials for diverse applications.
items.authors: Alexander Harjung, Chih-Chin Chi, Chuxuan Ling, Mariusz Matyszewski, Nino Makasarashvili, Lisa Kain

items.title: Do topological and quantum-inspired molecularrepresentations add value? Evidence from Africannatural-product-inspired antimalarial chemical space
items.authors: Myke Vital Sao Temgoua, Jean-Pierre TCHAPET NJAFA, Serge Guy Nana Engo, Penabei Samafou, Wilfred Fon Mbacham

items.title: Anomalous Hall Conductivity from Berry Curvature at the Dirac Point in AlPd5I2 Monolayer
items.abstract: The anomalous Hall effect (AHE) in non-magnetic materials is a powerful transport probe of the Berry curvature (BC) of Bloch electrons and a key component of next-generation spintronic devices. In this work, I present a first-principles study of the anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) in monolayer AlPd5I2, a two-dimensional material hosting a Dirac-type crossing located close to the Fermi energy. Density functional theory (DFT) with spin-orbit coupling (SOC) is performed using Quantum ESPRESSO and maximally localized Wannier functions (Wannier90). The electronic structure reveals a Dirac point at the S point, split by SOC into a gapped state with a large BC. The Fermi level is located slightly above the gap, yielding a metallic state with a very high AHC. The AHE is traced directly to the intense BC hotspots at the SOC-induced gap at the Dirac point. My findings establish the AlPd5I2 monolayer as a promising system for investigating BC dominated transport and large Hall responses.
items.authors: Shubham Sharma

items.title: Historical Side Information and the Reversal of Open-System Dynamics
items.abstract: Microscopic reversibility guarantees the existence of a time-reversed trajectory for a globally reversible dynamical system, but does not by itself guarantee that a later controller possesses the physical information required to identify and implement that trajectory. For an open system, distinctions between different microscopic histories may become encoded in environmental correlations whose physical carriers disperse, degrade, or become inaccessible, even though the corresponding information remains present in the global state. We formulate this distinction in terms of the physically accessible state of the controller and introduce a task-dependent measure of historical reversal information: the additional physically realizable information required to achieve a prescribed reversal accuracy. For continuous systems, a local Gaussian model yields a rate–distortion lower benchmark whose high-resolution behavior separates a geometrical contribution from a dynamical amplification term. For chaotic dynamics, the latter can acquire a Pesin-type form proportional to the relevant positive Lyapunov exponents. We then distinguish practical loss of accessibility from causal inaccessibility. When carriers of reversal-relevant information cross a causal horizon, subsequent information backflow to the controller is excluded. Finally, we consider a finite physical memory and show, in a minimal model, that memory saturation followed by logical erasure links the loss of accessible historical distinctions to Landauer entropy production. If the corresponding erasure heat is transferred across a horizon, this yields a lower bound on the associated horizon-entropy and area increase. The resulting framework separates global information preservation from local physical recoverability and shows how openness, dynamical instability, finite record capacity, and causal structure can jointly limit the reversal of a particular realized history without violating microscopic reversibility.
items.authors: Paolo Ghigna

items.title: N-Phosphoryl Imines Enable Intermolecular Aza Paternò–Büchi Reactions with Unactivated and Activated Alkenes
items.abstract: Intermolecular aza Paternò–Büchi (aPB) reactions provide a direct and convergent approach to azetidines through the photocycloaddition of imines and alkenes. However, reactions involving unactivated alkenes remain challenging, particularly with acyclic imines, whose excited states are susceptible to rapid nonradiative relaxation and competing photochemical pathways. Here, we report N-phosphinyl imines as readily accessible and stable photoreactive partners for visiblelight-mediated intermolecular aPB reactions with unactivated alkenes. Triplet sensitization using thioxanthone as an inexpensive organic photocatalyst enables productive [2+2]-cycloaddition across a range of alkenes, establishing a new reagent platform for intermolecular aPB chemistry to expand the accessible reactivity of acyclic imines with unactivated alkenes.
items.authors: Scott L. Kim, Lillian J. Carleu, Corinna S. Schindler

items.title: Nickel-Catalyzed Formal [3+2+2] Cycloadditions of Bis(trimethylsilyl)cyclopropanone withDiynes: A Concise Approach to Functionalized Azulene Derivatives
items.abstract: consequently, developing efficient methods for their preparation is important. Herein, we report the development of formal [3+2+2] cycloaddition chemistry involving 1,6-diynes and cis-2,3-bis(trimethylsilyl)cyclopropanone as a new synthetic approach to functionalized azulene derivatives. The azulene framework is efficiently constructed using the developed reaction, with synthetically versatile functional groups introduced in a single operation.
